meta.title: The Cold War: A World History
meta.author: Odd Arne Westad

chapters.title: The Cold War and Latin America
The World the Cold War Made

segments.note: Already a continent-spanning empire in the 1890s, closing fast on Europe's leading powers.
A Spanish colony until 1898, then under American control and counterinsurgency.
Formally independent, yet under heavy American control and repeated US occupation.
Castro's radical nationalist revolution takes power, at first courting US investors and not yet Soviet-aligned.
As ties with Washington collapse, Castro turns to Moscow; Mikoyan's visit brings Soviet credits and an oil-for-sugar deal.
Its Soviet patron disappears as the USSR is dissolved.
A CIA-funded campaign elects Frei over Allende; Chile stays in the US orbit, though Frei is no pliant ally.
Allende's Socialist-Communist coalition seeks a peaceful road to socialism; Moscow funds it but doubts it will survive.
Pinochet's coup brings a fiercely anti-Communist dictatorship that Washington quickly offers to help.
Until 1979 Nicaragua is run by a deeply unpopular dictatorship propped up by the United States.
The victorious Sandinistas look to Havana and the Soviet camp for close partnership.
The regional peace plan brings free elections in 1990, ending the Sandinistas' Soviet-leaning rule.
Árbenz's elected reformist government, backed by the tiny Guatemalan Communist Party, pursues land reform against US company interests.
A CIA-organized invasion topples Árbenz; US-blessed military juntas take over and reverse his reforms.
Argentina refuses to side with the Allies; Washington embargoes it and breaks relations in 1944.
The Videla junta casts its dirty war as a front in the global anti-Communist struggle, confident of US ties.
Britain sits atop the late-1800s world order, resented as a rival by rising Russia and America.
France, holder of a huge overseas empire, is one of Europe's leading imperial powers.
Bismarck's unified German state is strengthening its place in Europe's great-power system.
Hitler takes power and turns Germany into a one-party Nazi dictatorship.
After unconditional surrender, defeated Germany is placed under Allied occupation zones.
Currency reform and Marshall aid tie the western zones to the US-led economy, splitting them from the Soviet zone.
One of Europe's established monarchies of the imperial era; its king is killed by an anarchist in 1900.
Mussolini's Fascists make Italy a one-party state, a collectivist rival to liberal capitalism.
Allied landings knock Italy out of the Axis, and it changes sides.
Salazar's authoritarian Portugal stays neutral in the war, which lets the regime outlive 1945.
Authoritarian Portugal, no wartime ally, is admitted to NATO because of its Atlantic island bases.
As the Germans withdraw, Britain installs a coalition government and later bombs Communist positions in Athens.
Tsarist Russia, a vast land empire built by conquest, ranks among the great powers of the imperial age.
The Bolshevik seizure of power creates a Soviet state that defies the capitalist world.
The USSR is dissolved; Yeltsin's Russia and the other republics emerge as separate states, and the Soviet camp is gone.
Parts of Poland have been under Russian imperial rule since the eighteenth century.
A reborn Poland beats back the Red Army and later relies on defense pacts with Britain and France.
Moscow sets up a provisional government in Warsaw, bypassing the London exiles; Communists run it under Soviet tutelage.
Solidarity's Mazowiecki forms a non-Communist government and Moscow accepts it, ending Poland's place in the Soviet bloc.
The interwar republic looks to Britain and France, who then abandon it to Germany in 1938.
Freed from German occupation and run by a coalition, Czechoslovakia is not yet assumed to be in Moscow's sphere.
Communists force President Beneš to appoint a government entirely under their control.
The velvet revolution brings multiparty democracy and the dissident Havel to the presidency.
Before 1918 Hungary is a core part of Austria-Hungary, the empire dominating central Europe.
Austria-Hungary disintegrates at war's end, leaving Hungary a separate, weakened state.
Hungarian forces join the German assault on the USSR.
After the siege of Budapest, Hungary falls under Red Army occupation and Soviet political direction.
Hungary dissolves its Communist Party and people's republic and schedules free elections, with Moscow's blessing.
Moscow and the German Communists create the GDR inside the Soviet occupation zone.
Welcomed as liberators, the Soviets back Communist-held Yugoslavia, which stays loyal to Moscow through 1947.
Expelled from the Cominform, Tito defies Stalin and his regime survives outside the Soviet bloc.
Enlarged after 1918 and tied to Britain and France; it helps crush Hungary’s Communists in 1919.
Romanian troops fight alongside Germany in the invasion of the Soviet Union.
Romania switches sides late; a million Red Army troops take full military control.
Nominally in the Warsaw Pact, Ceauşescu's Romania condemns the Czechoslovak invasion and flaunts its independence from Moscow.
Ceauşescu's violent overthrow and execution finish Communist rule in Romania.
The Baltic lands are provinces of the Tsarist empire until its collapse.
The Baltic republics break away from the old empire; Poland's 1920 victory secures their independence.
The Nazi-Soviet pact lets Stalin occupy and absorb the Baltic states.
Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania restore full independence during the failed Moscow coup.
Westad counts China's subjugation among Europe's imperial feats; the Boxers later rise against foreign influence.
Fighting Japan, Nationalist China becomes a US ally and one of the five veto powers of the new UN.
Mao proclaims the People's Republic and immediately seeks a formal pact with Moscow.
Khrushchev recalls Soviet experts; Mao embraces the break and China becomes a Communist power standing alone.
Chiang's defeated Nationalists retreat to the island, keeping an anti-Communist Chinese government alive.
Japan is building up its position in East Asia and defeats Russia in 1905 with British backing.
Waging war on China since 1937 and allied with Germany, Japan belongs to the Axis camp.
Sole US occupation under MacArthur, excluding the Soviets, sets out to remake Japan as a dependable American ally.
Korea is an old kingdom long bound to Qing China.
Dominant since China's 1895 defeat, Japan annexes Korea outright and tries to stamp out Korean identity.
US forces occupy the south and come to rely on Syngman Rhee.
The Red Army occupies the north above the 38th parallel and picks Kim Il-sung to lead it.
Its Soviet patron disappears as the USSR is dissolved.
Under British rule; the Indian National Congress is among the first anticolonial organizations.
Freed from British rule, Nehru's India styles itself anticolonial, socialist and outside both power blocs.
Partition creates Pakistan as a separate Muslim state, immediately at odds with India over Kashmir.
Pakistan courts Washington; a 1954 military aid pact, then SEATO and the Baghdad Pact, bind it to the West.
The Dutch East Indies, a colony pieced together by the Netherlands during the 1800s.
Sukarno proclaims an independent Indonesia; four years of struggle against the returning Dutch follow.
The army crushes the PKI and sidelines Sukarno, opening three decades of right-wing, US-friendly rule.
Part of French-colonized Southeast Asia at the height of European dominance.
Ho's Communist-led Viet Minh proclaims independence and soon fights the returning French while still courting Washington.
Ho's Viet Minh joins the Communist camp; once war breaks out in Korea, Chinese Communist aid to it becomes plain.
Out of Cambodia, Vietnam normalizes ties with China and joins ASEAN's amity treaty, a Communist state without a Soviet patron.
The Geneva settlement leaves a separate southern state that soon leans entirely on American aid.
Part of French Indochina.
Independent under its king, Sihanouk, who tries to keep the country out of the Indochina wars.
With Sihanouk ousted and exiled in Beijing, US and South Vietnamese forces strike into Cambodia.
The Maoist-inspired Khmer Rouge seize Cambodia and pursue autarky and mass murder, loosely tied to China, not Moscow.
Vietnam's invasion topples Pol Pot and installs a pro-Hanoi regime in Cambodia.
With outside backing for both sides running out, the Cambodian war ends in a 1991 settlement.
A neutral monarchy that Khrushchev courts with aid during his tour of South Asia.
A Marxist military coup brings Afghan Communists to power, working closely with Soviet advisers.
The Communist regime falls as mujahedin factions storm Kabul and turn their guns on each other.
Westad calls the post-9/11 US occupation the making of a twenty-first-century colony under an unwilling great power.
Part of the Arab world subjugated by Europe; Egypt is under British occupation.
The Free Officers topple the king; Nasser practises a nonalignment that leans ever more on Soviet aid.
After the 1967 defeat, Soviet rearmament and thousands of Soviet military personnel make Egypt Moscow's nearest non-Warsaw Pact ally.
Sadat expels many Soviet advisers and quietly opens channels to Washington.
After the October War, Sadat's Egypt defects to the American side in search of a US-brokered peace.
Both superpowers back Israel's creation; Moscow even hopes the new state might lean its way.
Ben-Gurion sides fully with Britain and France at Suez, then moves closer to Washington.
Independent but pressed by empires; its elites, like those of China and Japan, hope to build a modern industrial state.
British and Soviet forces occupy Iran, the Soviets holding the north, to secure oil and block Germany.
After US pressure forces a Soviet pullout, Tehran retakes the north and crushes Soviet-backed separatists.
Mossadegh's nationalist government, anti-Soviet but defiant of Britain, takes over the oil industry.
After the CIA-British coup the Shah rules for twenty-six years as a close American ally.
Khomeini's Islamic republic deliberately turns its back on both East and West.
Carved from the Ottoman lands and run as a British-dominated client state.
Monarchist Iraq is a US ally and a pillar of the Baghdad Pact security system.
The bloody 1958 revolution turns Iraq from a key US ally into a partner of Nasser and Moscow.
Qasim is overthrown and killed; anti-Communist Ba'athists rise despite Soviet disapproval.
Ba'athist Iraq, soon dominated by Saddam Hussein, relies on Soviet and East European security and economic aid.
Saddam's Iraq attacks Iran over Soviet objections; Washington, more worried about Iran, tilts quietly toward Baghdad.
The US occupation of Iraq is, for Westad, the second such colony created by Bush's lashing out.
Placed under French control after the Ottoman collapse.
French control fades and Arab nationalists come to dominate Syrian politics.
Moscow embraces the radical Ba'athist regime in Damascus and expands arms deliveries.
Its Soviet patron disappears as the USSR is dissolved.
French North Africa, where jihadist peasant movements resist Western rule.
The FLN takes power as a radical anticolonial regime meant to embody the Third World.
The Gold Coast, a British colony.
Independent under Nkrumah, Ghana joins the Third World camp while seeking Soviet cooperation.
Officers who topple Nkrumah set up a military regime closely tied to the United States.
Belgian-ruled Congo, prized for its minerals.
Independence under Lumumba, a radical nationalist distrusted by Washington and Brussels.
After the army ousts Lumumba, Congo falls under a US-supported military dictatorship.
A Portuguese colony.
The MPLA proclaims a People's Republic, secured by Cuban troops and Soviet arms and advisers.
Its Soviet patron disappears as the USSR is dissolved.
An independent empire, one of very few African states never colonised for long.
Mengistu's Dergue courts the Soviet bloc; by 1977 Moscow arms it and Cuba sends advisers, then troops.
Its Soviet patron disappears as the USSR is dissolved.
Under British and settler rule; the African National Congress soon emerges as an early anticolonial body.
A self-governing, white-ruled dominion inside the British empire; later a firm anti-Communist partner of the West.

events.title: Marx's Communist Manifesto
events.note: Marx lays out the case for proletarian revolution and state ownership of production; his followers take the name Communists from the tract.

events.title: Crimean War
events.note: A British-led coalition curbs Russia's grip on the Black Sea region, leaving many Russians convinced that Britain is bent on thwarting their rise.

events.title: German unification under Bismarck
events.note: Many German workers welcome Bismarck's new unitary state, preferring nation-building to class struggle, while Marx denounces it as military despotism.

events.title: Indian National Congress founded
events.note: Educated Indian elites form one of the earliest organized anticolonial bodies, turning ideas borrowed from the imperial metropole against colonial rule.

events.title: Barings crisis sparks global depression
events.note: Risky foreign lending nearly sinks a major London bank; economic interdependence spreads the shock into the first worldwide capitalist crisis, with mass unemployment and labor unrest.

events.title: German Social Democrats' Erfurt program
events.note: The SPD makes democracy and equal suffrage its central aims, drawing Engels's scorn as opportunism; reformists and Marxist radicals start to diverge.

events.title: Wave of anarchist assassinations
events.note: Amid the 1890s slump, anarchists bomb and kill rulers: France's president in 1894, Italy's king in 1900 and US President McKinley in 1901.

events.title: Tonghak peasant rebellion
events.note: Korean peasant rebels oppose Western influence, one of several popular movements that Westad sees as sowing later anticolonial resistance.

events.title: First Sino-Japanese War
events.note: China's defeat ends Qing influence over Korea and opens the peninsula to Japanese expansion.

events.title: Spanish-American War
events.note: A brief victorious war and the counterinsurgencies that follow in Cuba and the Philippines drive a leap in US military spending and overseas reach.

events.title: US war in the Philippines
events.note: America's first colonial venture in Asia meets resistance uniting Filipino patricians and peasants.

events.title: Reformists and revolutionaries split
events.note: Radicals denounce Denmark's 1899 labor compromise as betrayal; Westad dates the lasting rift between reformist Social Democrats and future Communists to this decade.

events.title: Boxer Uprising
events.note: Chinese peasant militants rise against foreign influence, part of a wider wave of popular resistance to Western power.

events.title: Bolshevik-Menshevik split
events.note: Meeting in exile in London, Russia's Social Democrats divide into Bolsheviks and Mensheviks, partly over Lenin's push for personal control of the party.

events.title: Russo-Japanese War
events.note: Russians widely credit British support for Japan's 1905 victory, deepening their view of Britain as the main obstacle to Russian ascendance.

events.title: Russian Revolution of 1905
events.note: Protests wring an elected Duma from the tsar; Trotsky leads the capital's soviet, while Lenin rejects elections as a road to socialism.

events.title: Taft's dollar diplomacy
events.note: Taft, once governor of the conquered Philippines, casts American capital as a civilizing force abroad and pledges that Washington will shield US firms doing business in Latin America and Asia.

events.title: Japan annexes Korea
events.note: Korea becomes part of the Japanese Empire; Tokyo demolishes the royal palace, imposes Japanese in higher education and keeps Koreans segregated.

events.title: African National Congress founded
events.note: South Africans create one of the earliest anticolonial organizations, which later becomes the main vehicle of the struggle against apartheid.

events.title: World War I begins
events.note: Westad treats it as the start of three decades of European civil war: over fifteen million dead, empires gone, and the cauldron of both Communist power and Fascism.

events.title: Tsar overthrown
events.note: Russia's monarchy falls, but the liberal-socialist government that follows can neither exit the war nor cope with its economic ruin.

events.title: US enters World War I
events.note: German submarine warfare pushes Wilson to join the Allies, framing the war as a crusade for democracy, justice and free commerce.

events.title: Bolshevik Revolution
events.note: Lenin's Bolsheviks seize Petrograd and Moscow in a coup, founding the first Communist state and a permanent challenge to world capitalism.

events.title: Wilson's Fourteen Points
events.note: Wilson presents US war aims as a just peace built on national self-government and a League of Nations, an internationalism rivaling Lenin's.

events.title: Lenin makes separate peace with Germany
events.note: Lenin takes Russia out of the war against Germany while calling for revolution across Europe, horrifying the governments that had fought alongside the tsar.

events.title: Russian Civil War
events.note: The Reds defeat the Whites at a cost of two million lives; Westad credits real popular support and the Whites' reliance on tsarist officers.

events.title: Allied intervention in Russia
events.note: Western troops enter Russia, first to keep the eastern front alive, then against the Bolsheviks; the failed effort lets Lenin pose as Russia's defender.

events.title: World War I ends; empires collapse
events.note: The war closes in 1918 with the Habsburg and Ottoman empires gone and America the leading power; Poland, the Baltic republics and a shrunken Hungary emerge as separate states.

events.title: Paris Peace Conference
events.note: Korean exiles plead for self-determination in Paris and Rhee petitions Wilson, but Washington and London, wary of Tokyo, give them nothing.

events.title: Berlin left-wing rising crushed
events.note: Leftist socialists rise in Berlin and are crushed, their leaders including Liebknecht murdered; Bavaria's Soviet republic is defeated that May.

events.title: Comintern founded
events.note: Lenin sets up the Third International, binding new Communist parties everywhere to centralized Soviet leadership and, over time, to Soviet foreign policy.

events.title: Hungarian Soviet Republic
events.note: Hungary's Communists outlast every other postwar Soviet regime until Romanian troops with French and British backing crush them in August; Moscow cannot help.

events.title: Korean independence rising
events.note: Disappointed hopes of self-determination spark a Korean revolt, which Japan suppresses at great cost in Korean lives.

events.title: US Red Scare
events.note: Fear of Bolshevism sweeps America: suspected radicals are arrested and deported, free speech is curbed, and federal power helps employers crush strikes.

events.title: League of Nations founded
events.note: Wilson's world body is born, but Washington soon drops his dream of reshaping Europe through it, even as US trade and culture spread abroad.

events.title: Short-lived Soviet republic in northern Iran
events.note: A Soviet republic proclaimed in Iran's north soon collapses, and Iranian Communists go underground to build labor unions and city networks.

events.title: Polish-Soviet War
events.note: A costly, badly fought Soviet war loses former imperial land to Poland and forestalls Soviet moves against the Baltic republics.

events.title: Lenin's New Economic Policy
events.note: With the economy wrecked and grain being seized from peasants, Lenin briefly allows market incentives; Westad calls it a tactical move, dropped once it had delivered quick results.

events.title: Chinese Communist Party founded
events.note: China's small Communist Party is founded and cooperates with Sun Yat-sen's much larger Guomindang nationalists.

events.title: South African Communist Party founded
events.note: Formed the same year as China's party, it urges workers of every race to overthrow capitalism; it later works inside the ANC and supplies many anti-apartheid leaders.

events.title: Mussolini's Fascists take power in Italy
events.note: Born of the Great War's upheaval, Mussolini's Fascists pitch a blend of nationalism and socialism against liberal capitalism and make Italy a one-party state, a model Hitler later follows.

events.title: Soviet Union founded
events.note: The Russian Soviet republic becomes the core of a Bolshevik-ruled federation of republics carved from the former empire.

events.title: Hitler's Munich putsch
events.note: Hitler's first grab for power fails, but his party goes on to exploit nationalism, anticapitalism and anti-Semitism against the Weimar Republic.

events.title: Lenin dies; Stalin rises
events.note: After Lenin's death, general secretary Stalin outmaneuvers all rivals, including Trotsky, and by 1928 is the unchallenged master of party and state.

events.title: Brussels anti-imperialist congress
events.note: A Comintern-arranged meeting of anticolonial activists, Nehru among them, escapes its sponsors' control and turns into a denunciation of European rule.

events.title: Havana conference protests US interventions
events.note: Mexico, Argentina and others condemn the string of US armed interventions across Central America and the Caribbean islands.

events.title: Comintern's 'social fascism' line
events.note: Until 1935 Moscow brands Social Democrats as fascists, blocking a united front against Hitler; young socialists such as Willy Brandt blame the Communists.

events.title: Wall Street crash
events.note: The crash opens the Great Depression; as world output falls about fifteen percent, Communism wins wide sympathy as an alternative to failing capitalism.

events.title: Collectivization and terror
events.note: Stalin's war on the kulaks forces land into state hands; his regime kills at least ten million people by 1953, and at least three million more die in the Ukrainian famine.

events.title: Hitler takes power
events.note: Riding Depression misery from under 3 to 37 percent of the vote, the Nazis take office and build a one-party state.

events.title: Roosevelt's Good Neighbor policy
events.note: After Latin protests at Havana in 1928, Roosevelt softens the US tone toward the southern republics, which later makes most of them readier to line up against the Axis.

events.title: Roosevelt's New Deal
events.note: Roosevelt uses planning and regulation to rescue capitalism from its critics on left and right, as Britain and France also expand welfare.

events.title: US recognizes the USSR
events.note: FDR opens diplomatic relations with Moscow, doing little more than Britain, France, Germany and Italy had done long before.

events.title: Spanish Civil War
events.note: Franco, aided by Hitler and Mussolini, defeats the Republic; Soviet advisers fight other leftists, and the democracies stay out.

events.title: Stalin's Great Purge
events.note: Stalin's terror turns on the party itself: close to a million are shot, among them almost every original Bolshevik leader, including Bukharin.

events.title: Stalin purges Korean Communists
events.note: Leading Korean Communists in Moscow are shot as supposed Japanese spies, and some 200,000 Soviet Koreans are deported to central Asia.

events.title: Japan launches full-scale war on China
events.note: Japan's all-out assault on China opens a war still grinding on four years later; it wrecks Chinese industry and sets Tokyo on the expansionist path that binds it to the Axis.

events.title: Munich betrayal of Czechoslovakia
events.note: Britain and France abandon Czechoslovakia to Germany; the memory of betrayal later feeds Czech support for Communism and Western sympathy in 1948.

events.title: Germany seizes Czech lands
events.note: After absorbing Austria, Hitler takes western Czechoslovakia unopposed; Stalin's bids for collective security with the Western powers come to nothing.

events.title: Nazi-Soviet Pact
events.note: Stalin makes a nonaggression deal with Hitler that divides eastern Europe into spheres, triggering the war and stunning opinion worldwide.

events.title: Germany invades Poland; WWII begins
events.note: Germany attacks on 1 September; bound by their pledge to Poland, Britain and France declare war two days later, and Soviet troops invade from the east.

events.title: Katyn massacre
events.note: Soviet secret police shoot some twenty-two thousand Polish officers and elites, one reason Moscow knows any free Polish vote would go against it.

events.title: Fall of France
events.note: The Phony War ends as Germany overruns the Low Countries, Denmark, Norway and France, leaving Britain alone and the Soviets seemingly on Berlin's side.

events.title: Soviets occupy the Baltic states
events.note: Under cover of his deal with Hitler, Stalin sends in the Red Army and absorbs Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia, ending two decades of independence.

events.title: Lend-Lease aid
events.note: Roosevelt puts US industry at Britain's service short of sending troops, later extending aid to the USSR; $11.3 billion in goods reaches Moscow by 1945.

events.title: Churchill pledges aid to Russia
events.note: Without naming Stalin, the lifelong anti-Communist promises British help to the Russian people, seeing Soviet resistance as Britain's best hope.

events.title: Germany invades the Soviet Union
events.note: Hitler breaks the pact and attacks; a stunned Stalin at first refuses to believe it, and by November German armies besiege Leningrad and near Moscow.

events.title: Anglo-Soviet occupation of Iran
events.note: British and Soviet troops occupy Iran to forestall German influence and control its oil, with Moscow holding the north.

events.title: Atlantic Charter
events.note: Roosevelt and Churchill pledge self-government for all peoples; Indian, Indonesian and Algerian nationalists insist the promise must cover the colonies too.

events.title: Germans halted before Moscow
events.note: Stubborn defense, overstretched supply lines and a brutal winter stop the German advance, transforming the war's international balance.

events.title: Germany declares war on the US
events.note: Hitler's rash declaration helps unite the strongest alliance in history against the Axis.

events.title: Pearl Harbor attack
events.note: Stalemate in Russia turns Japan southward; its surprise strike on the US fleet and European colonies brings America into the war.

events.title: Japan conquers Southeast Asia
events.note: Within six months Japan seizes the region and reaches India's borders; Sukarno cooperates with the new occupiers to escape Dutch rule.

events.title: Churchill's first Moscow visit
events.note: The arch anti-Communist and the head of world Communism reach practical agreements, though Stalin repeatedly scolds Britain for delaying a land offensive.

events.title: Quit India Movement
events.note: Rejecting Britain's offer of self-rule after the war, Gandhi launches a campaign to exploit wartime weakness and drive the British out now.

events.title: Soviet victory at Stalingrad
events.note: The Red Army breaks the German offensive; from mid-1943 Soviet forces push west on broad fronts and Moscow shifts from supplicant to demander.

events.title: Comintern dissolved
events.note: Moscow disbands the Communist International in mid-war as a goodwill gesture to its capitalist allies; it comes back in 1947 as the Cominform.

events.title: Allied landings in Italy
events.note: Allied troops land in Italy, but the second front in France that Stalin keeps demanding still has not come.

events.title: Cairo Conference
events.note: The Allied leaders pledge that Korea will regain its independence after Japan's defeat.

events.title: Tehran Conference
events.note: Meeting Stalin privately, FDR accepts moving Poland west and Soviet annexation of the Baltics, asking only for secrecy, and wins a promise of war on Japan.

events.title: D-Day: second front opens
events.note: The Western Allies finally land in France; to Stalin, waiting until nine million Soviet soldiers had died proves Anglo-American bad faith.

events.title: Baltic and Ukrainian anti-Soviet insurgencies
events.note: As the Red Army returns, Baltic and Ukrainian nationalist guerrillas fight Soviet rule for years; Moscow replies with mass arrests and deportations.

events.title: Soviet deportations of border peoples
events.note: Over a million Balts and Caucasians, among them the entire Chechen people, are shipped east as Moscow clears border regions of suspect groups.

events.title: Washington breaks with Argentina
events.note: Argentina, which declined to side with the Allies, is embargoed and loses US recognition; it declares war only in March 1945.

events.title: Bretton Woods agreements
events.note: Allied industrial nations create the IMF and a reconstruction bank and fix currencies to the dollar, legitimizing America's economic supremacy.

events.title: Romania switches sides
events.note: With Hitler's war going badly, young King Michael dismisses the pro-German regime and Romania changes sides; a million Red Army soldiers soon hold the country.

events.title: Warsaw Uprising
events.note: The Red Army halts outside Warsaw while the Germans destroy the Home Army and the city; Stalin wants as few Polish officers alive as possible.

events.title: Athens clashes; British fight ELAS
events.note: Police fire on a leftist rally, ELAS strikes back and British planes bomb Communist strongholds; on Soviet advice Greek Communists disband their army in 1945.

events.title: Soviet-made Polish government
events.note: Moscow creates a provisional government ignoring the London exiles; the Yalta-sanctioned coalition that follows has a nominal non-Communist majority but Communist control.

events.title: Red Army takes Budapest
events.note: After a ruinous siege the Hungarian capital falls to Soviet forces during the Yalta talks; Hungary, too late in trying to switch sides, comes under Red Army occupation.

events.title: Yalta Conference
events.note: The Big Three fix Soviet entry into the Pacific war, UN membership and a French zone, accept a Communist-based Polish regime and sign a vague democracy pledge.

events.title: Soviets impose Romanian government
events.note: Soviet envoy Vyshinskii gives King Michael two hours to dismiss his cabinet, installing a coalition in which Communists control justice and the police.

events.title: US and Soviet troops meet at Elbe
events.note: American and Soviet soldiers embrace and sing together on the Elbe; Westad notes four decades would pass before such easy contact returned.

events.title: Roosevelt dies; Truman becomes president
events.note: FDR's sudden death puts an unprepared Truman, never involved in foreign policy, in charge; he sees Communism as a direct challenge to a US-led order.

events.title: Soviet-Polish treaty
events.note: Warsaw's Soviet-backed provisional government signs its main treaty with Moscow before the Yalta coalition takes office, letting Polish Communists cast the USSR as guarantor of statehood.

events.title: Stalin: armies impose their systems
events.note: Hosting Yugoslav Communists in Moscow, Stalin explains that in this war each victor will install its own social order wherever its troops stand.

events.title: Truman rebukes Molotov over Poland
events.note: Less than two weeks into his presidency, Truman bluntly tells the Soviet foreign minister that friendship depends on keeping the Yalta bargains.

events.title: Churchill's 'iron curtain' telegram
events.note: Churchill first uses the phrase in a message urging Truman to settle matters with Moscow before Western armies shrink; Truman declines to halt the withdrawal.

events.title: Hitler's suicide and German surrender
events.note: Hitler kills himself on 30 April and Germany surrenders unconditionally on 7 May as Allied armies close in from east, west and south.

events.title: Hopkins mission to Stalin
events.note: Truman sends FDR's dying confidant to Moscow to voice American misgivings; Stalin will not yield and blames the British for the trouble.

events.title: Lend-Lease to USSR cut off
events.note: Truman's abrupt end to aid after victory in Europe, chiefly a cost-cutting step, persuades Stalin that Washington's attitude has changed.

events.title: Red Army liberates Czechoslovakia
events.note: Soviet troops ending six years of German rule are cheered as fellow Slavs; a coalition governs, and few in the West yet assume the country belongs to Moscow's sphere.

events.title: Yugoslavs occupy Trieste
events.note: Yugoslav Communists seize the Italian port at war's end, one of the disputes that sour postwar Allied foreign-ministers' meetings.

events.title: Germany divided into four zones
events.note: Germany and Berlin are split into four zones; Stalin wants a neutral or socialist Germany and fears the West turning its richer part into an arsenal.

events.title: Red Army atrocities in Germany
events.note: Mass rape, looting and killing by Soviet troops, shrugged off by Stalin, cripple Moscow's ability to govern and leave a legacy of hatred.

events.title: Moscow show trial of Polish resistance leaders
events.note: Soviet police seize surviving chiefs of Poland's wartime underground and try them in Moscow; Stalin asks for mild sentences to please his allies, yet most die in custody.

events.title: United Nations founded
events.note: FDR's world body pairs a universal General Assembly with a five-power Security Council holding vetoes; Stalin and the British join mainly to please Washington.

events.title: Labour wins British election
events.note: Labour ousts Churchill; Stalin distrusts Attlee and Bevin, fearing their social-democratic welfare state as Communism's toughest rival in western Europe.

events.title: Potsdam Conference
events.note: With Truman new and Attlee replacing Churchill midway, the victors settle German occupation and Poland's western border but postpone the big questions; Truman hints at the bomb.

events.title: Atomic bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
events.note: The US destroys two Japanese cities, opening the nuclear age that Westad sees as a main reason the Cold War system endured.

events.title: Sukarno proclaims Indonesia
events.note: Having worked with the Japanese occupiers, Sukarno declares a sovereign state spanning the whole former Dutch colony.

events.title: Japan surrenders
events.note: Japan's collapse, alongside failing European empires, leaves Asia open to revolution; the US orders Japanese forces in China to surrender only to Chiang.

events.title: Korea divided at 38th parallel
events.note: Washington and Moscow split the peninsula into Soviet and American occupation zones, meant only to handle Japan's surrender; no one expects it to last.

events.title: Chiang-Stalin deal on Manchuria
events.note: Chiang's government grants the Soviets economic and military rights in Manchuria in return for Stalin recognizing Nationalist control there.

events.title: Soviet entry into war against Japan
events.note: Declaring war on 9 August, the Red Army sweeps through Manchuria, northern Korea and the islands north of Japan within three weeks.

events.title: US occupation of Japan
events.note: Truman keeps Japan under sole US control; MacArthur imposes demilitarization, a new constitution and sweeping New Deal-style reforms, while the emperor stays.

events.title: Ho Chi Minh proclaims Vietnam's independence
events.note: The Communist leader declares a state for all Viet-speaking lands France had colonized, naming himself president.

events.title: Communist surge in Western Europe
events.note: Communists win up to 29 percent in France and 19 in Italy and enter unity cabinets, but on Moscow's advice avoid revolutionary challenges.

events.title: Battle of Surabaya
events.note: British troops clearing the way for a Dutch return clash with Indonesian nationalists; about 600 British and over 9,000 Indonesians die.

events.title: Smallholders win Hungarian election
events.note: The Smallholders take over half the vote and the Communists 16 percent; Stalin has Voroshilov demand the interior ministry and extra deputy premierships for the Left.

events.title: Marshall mission to China
events.note: Truman sends General Marshall to broker a Nationalist-Communist settlement; Stalin tells the CCP to cooperate, but it refuses and fighting grows.

events.title: Kennan's Long Telegram
events.note: Diplomat George Kennan portrays Soviet policy as ideologically driven and expansionist yet cautious, urging a more forward US policy of containment.

events.title: Perón elected in Argentina
events.note: Westad calls US handling of Perón, the archetypal populist in American eyes, a template later applied to supposed Communist threats.

events.title: Iran crisis
events.note: Soviet troops overstay the deadline, backing Azeri and Kurdish republics; US pressure forces a May withdrawal, after which Tehran retakes the north and executes separatist leaders.

events.title: Churchill's Iron Curtain speech
events.note: Introduced by Truman at Fulton, Missouri, Churchill publicly warns that an iron curtain now splits Europe and Soviet control is growing behind it.

events.title: Soviets withdraw from Manchuria
events.note: Under US pressure, Stalin suddenly pulls the Red Army out, giving Mao's forces the military upper hand in Manchuria.

events.title: Syria freed of French rule
events.note: The last French and British troops leave Syria, where Arab nationalists now set the political tone as European control over the region recedes.

events.title: SED formed in the Soviet zone
events.note: Soviet occupiers and German Communists push eastern Social Democrats into a merged Socialist Unity Party run by Pieck and Ulbricht; many Social Democrats relocate west rather than submit.

events.title: US zone halts reparations to Moscow
events.note: General Clay unilaterally stops sending reparations to the Soviets from the American-run zone; Britain follows three months later, and an angry Moscow can do nothing about it.

events.title: Czechoslovak Communists top free vote
events.note: Communists take 38 percent in a free election, the strongest result in east-central Europe, fed by distrust of the West after 1938.

events.title: Chinese civil war
events.note: Chiang's US-armed offensive nearly succeeds, but the Soviet-aided PLA traps his armies in Manchuria while peasants, landlords and the middle class desert his regime.

events.title: Greek civil war flares again
events.note: Renewed fighting between Communist guerrillas and the government prompts a financially strained Britain to ask Washington to take over its role.

events.title: Polish referendum
events.note: Communists secure, by fair means and foul, a majority for land reform and nationalizing basic industry, while sidelining their coalition partners.

events.title: Soviet postwar famine
events.note: Parts of the war-ravaged USSR go hungry, unreported by Soviet media, while Stalin keeps a rigid wartime command economy geared to heavy industry.

events.title: Paris foreign ministers' deadlock
events.note: Bevin and Molotov trade barbs as the allies deadlock over German reparations, peace treaties and Trieste; Truman declares himself tired of coddling Moscow.

events.title: Soviet demands on Turkey
events.note: New Soviet pressure over the Black Sea Straits feeds Truman's fear that Moscow is reaching for the eastern Mediterranean.

events.title: Rigged Romanian election
events.note: The Communist-led coalition wins a vote marked by widespread intimidation and fraud.

events.title: Republicans win Congress
events.note: Republicans capture Congress, their first majority in fourteen years, after attacking Truman as too generous abroad and too soft on Stalin.

events.title: Anglo-American Bizonia formed
events.note: After halting reparation deliveries to the Soviets, the Americans and British fuse their German zones economically, paving the way toward a distinct West German state.

events.title: First Indochina War
events.note: France fights to reclaim Indochina; once Korea erupts and Beijing aids the Viet Minh, Truman and then Eisenhower back the French effort.

events.title: Iran crushes Soviet-backed northern republics
events.note: With the Red Army gone, Premier Qavam breaks his pledges to Moscow; Iranian troops reoccupy the north and publicly execute Azeri and Kurdish leaders, badly weakening the Tudeh.

events.title: Rigged Polish election
events.note: Through fraud, coercion and barred candidates, the Communist-led bloc claims over 80 percent; Western reminders about free elections change nothing.

events.title: Britain asks US to take over Greece
events.note: Its economy faltering, Britain's Labour government formally asks Washington for help in Greece and Turkey, aiming to make America back London's Mediterranean position with deeds.

events.title: Moscow foreign ministers' conference
events.note: Great-power talks on Germany fail; Washington and London drift toward building up their own part of Germany, as Kennan had urged in 1945.

events.title: Truman Doctrine
events.note: Seeking $400 million for Greece and Turkey, Truman vows to back free peoples against subjugation, deliberately frightening Congress into approval.

events.title: French Communists expelled from government
events.note: The PCF is pushed out of the cabinet after opposing the reconquest of Indochina; Stalin later faults it for not quitting on its own terms.

events.title: Marshall Plan announced
events.note: Marshall offers over $12 billion for European recovery; western Europe accepts eagerly, while Stalin suspects a trap to lock in US hegemony and control of western Germany.

events.title: Dutch 'police actions' in Indonesia
events.note: The Netherlands tries to crush the young republic by force; Britain refuses support and Washington hesitates over the risk to its Dutch ally.

events.title: Molotov walks out of Paris talks
events.note: Stalin sends Molotov with a big delegation, then orders him out after a few days; Molotov warns the plan will split Europe under American dominance.

events.title: NSC and CIA created
events.note: Truman sets up the National Security Council and the CIA to coordinate Cold War policy and run espionage and covert operations.

events.title: Stalin bars Czechoslovakia from Marshall aid
events.note: Stalin berates Czechoslovak premier Gottwald for accepting the Paris invitation; Moscow tells every eastern government that US aid counts as an anti-Soviet act.

events.title: Rigged Hungarian election
events.note: Having decimated their partners through arrests and intimidation, Rákosi's Communists and allies claim 60 percent, and Stalin blesses the new regime.

events.title: India and Pakistan independent
events.note: Unable to afford empire and a welfare state at once, Attlee's Britain lets India and Pakistan go as it retreats from east of Suez.

events.title: Cominform founded
events.note: Reviving the Comintern in new form, Zhdanov denounces American imperialism, and Yugoslav delegates, at Soviet urging, lash French and Italian Communists for parliamentarism.

events.title: First Kashmir war
events.note: Kashmir joins India, a short war leaves it split about two to one, and Nehru, whose family came from there, will not surrender it.

events.title: US 'Plan Broiler' war plan
events.note: The Joint Chiefs draft one of their first full plans for war with the USSR, envisaging 34 atomic bombs on 24 Soviet cities.

events.title: UN backs partition of Palestine
events.note: The General Assembly recommends dividing Palestine, with Washington and Moscow both voting in favor; Jewish leaders proclaim their state the following May.

events.title: King Michael forced to abdicate
events.note: The Communist-led government pushes the young king off the throne and proclaims a People's Republic of Romania.

events.title: Stalin rebukes Balkan federation plan
events.note: At a hastily called Moscow meeting Stalin berates Yugoslav and Bulgarian leaders over their union plans, then pulls all Soviet advisers out of Yugoslavia.

events.title: Communist coup in Czechoslovakia
events.note: Threatening civil war and Soviet intervention, Communists force Beneš to accept their government; the shock turns western European socialists firmly against Moscow.

events.title: London conference on Germany
events.note: Meeting without the Soviets, the Western powers settle on German currency reform and elections in their zones; France joins reluctantly.

events.title: Brussels Pact
events.note: France, Britain and the Benelux states pledge mutual defense, but French leaders soon decide only an American commitment will do.

events.title: Italian election
events.note: With CIA funds and Vatican support, De Gasperi's Christian Democrats beat Togliatti's Communist-led front: the Agency's first large covert operation.

events.title: Jeju uprising crushed
events.note: Rhee's forces put down a Communist-led island revolt, executing suspected guerrillas, their families and sometimes entire villages.

events.title: OEEC set up to run Marshall aid
events.note: Created to administer American assistance across borders, the organization also dismantles trade quotas and pushes currency convertibility, an early seed of European integration.

events.title: First Arab-Israeli war
events.note: Israel defeats the invading Arab armies and takes much land meant for Palestinian Arabs; Jordan and Egypt take the West Bank and Gaza.

events.title: State of Israel declared
events.note: After the UN partition vote, Truman recognizes Israel over his advisers' objections, and Stalin backs it mainly to damage Britain's Middle East position.

events.title: Separate elections in southern Korea
events.note: Washington yields to Rhee and allows southern-only elections, sealing the division; Rhee, already persecuting the left, wins easily.

events.title: Berlin blockade and airlift
events.note: Stalin cuts land links to West Berlin; a US-British airlift supplies the city for almost a year. Westad judges it a Soviet failure that turned Germans against Moscow.

events.title: Deutschmark introduced
events.note: The new western currency empties the black market and refills shops, forcing the Soviets to issue their own money and sealing Germany's split.

events.title: US 'reverse course' in Japan
events.note: After Kennan's visit, Washington halts reform, eases the purge of wartime leaders and backs conservatives, while leftists are purged from jobs.

events.title: Malayan Emergency
events.note: British forces fight a Communist-led uprising in Malaya with American support while US troops help Manila crush the Huk rebellion; by 1954 both insurgencies are defeated.

events.title: Tito-Stalin split
events.note: The Cominform expels Yugoslavia and urges Tito's overthrow; he fights back and survives. Westad calls it a needless clash born of Stalin's paranoia, the first open Communist rift.

events.title: Republic of Korea proclaimed
events.note: Syngman Rhee declares the Republic of Korea in Seoul with American blessing.

events.title: North Korea proclaimed
events.note: Kim declares the Democratic People's Republic of Korea in Pyongyang; Soviet and US troops leave the peninsula soon afterward.

events.title: Madiun Communist uprising
events.note: An ill-fated Indonesian Communist revolt against the republic's leaders reassures Washington that it can back the nationalists.

events.title: Truman wins 1948 election
events.note: Truman narrowly defeats Dewey; Henry Wallace's left-wing campaign against the Cold War line wins only 2.5 percent.

events.title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
events.note: Backed by American liberals, western Europeans and new postcolonial states, the declaration passes while the Soviet bloc abstains; Westad calls it a US win over Soviet notions of rights.

events.title: NATO founded
events.note: Western governments rush to sign the North Atlantic Treaty in Washington; its main early effect is psychological, assuring Europeans the Americans will stay.

events.title: 'Loss of China' debate
events.note: Shocked Americans blame Chinese ingratitude, and Republicans such as Nixon accuse Truman's Democrats of losing China and harboring Communists at home.

events.title: Tito turns to the West for aid
events.note: Threatened by Stalin, who twice weighs an invasion, Tito reluctantly turns to Washington and the western Europeans, whose backing keeps his regime alive.

events.title: First Soviet atomic bomb test
events.note: Stalin's crash program, helped by spies inside the US project, ends the American nuclear monopoly and sets off an arms race.

events.title: Federal Republic of Germany founded
events.note: The West German state is launched with Adenauer as chancellor; Westad stresses that he wanted reunification, but valued anchoring his country in the West even more.

events.title: Stalin vetoes Kim's invasion plan
events.note: Stalin rejects one of Kim's proposals to attack the south, judging it unready and liable to invite American interference.

events.title: German Democratic Republic founded
events.note: Soviets and German Communists set up a state in their zone on the basis of the division the currency reform had created; Grotewohl stresses reconstruction.

events.title: Nehru's first meeting with Truman
events.note: Truman comes away convinced Nehru dislikes white men; Nehru sees the US as an immature, missionary superpower, and relations stay cool.

events.title: People's Republic of China proclaimed
events.note: Mao declares a people's republic in Beijing on the pattern of the Soviet satellites, against Moscow's advice to go slowly.

events.title: Rajk show trial in Hungary
events.note: Hungarian Communist László Rajk is branded a Titoist spy and shot, one of many independent-minded Communists purged after the Yugoslav break.

events.title: Chiang retreats to Taiwan
events.note: Beaten on the mainland, Chiang Kai-shek and his Nationalist government flee to the island.

events.title: Dutch concede Indonesian independence
events.note: When the Dutch arrest republican leaders, the US threatens to cut economic aid and backs a UN demand to restore them; the Netherlands gives way.

events.title: Communist China backs the Viet Minh
events.note: Mao's victory gives Ho a Communist patron next door; as the Korean War rages, Chinese help to the Viet Minh becomes obvious, and Washington now treats Indochina as a Cold War front.

events.title: Klaus Fuchs arrested
events.note: The physicist who passed US nuclear secrets to Moscow is arrested in Britain; secret Venona decrypts expose many other Soviet agents.

events.title: McCarthy's State Department accusations
events.note: Senator Joseph McCarthy claims Communists work inside the State Department, launching a witch hunt that Westad says hurt the US more than Soviet spying did.

events.title: Sino-Soviet alliance treaty
events.note: Mao goes to Moscow in December 1949 and wins an alliance from a grudging Stalin, who distrusts the CCP's peasant roots and independent rise.

events.title: Kim in Moscow gets Stalin's approval
events.note: Emboldened by the Chinese Communist victory and US passivity, Stalin approves an invasion but makes Kim seek Mao's consent, a test of Chinese loyalty.

events.title: NSC-68 strategy paper
events.note: Paul Nitze's paper calls for huge defense budgets and global intervention against a Soviet foe it paints as bent on world domination; the Korean War makes it policy.

events.title: Kim in Beijing wins Mao's backing
events.note: After checking that Stalin really agreed, a reluctant Mao endorses the attack but warns Kim that imperialist intervention could complicate it.

events.title: Schuman Declaration
events.note: France's foreign minister proposes merging French and German coal and steel output under a common authority so that a new war between the two becomes impossible.

events.title: Revolutionary terror in China
events.note: Copying Stalin's 1930s quotas, the new regime crushes rural elites and the bourgeoisie and expels foreign influence; nearly two million die in two years.

events.title: North Korea invades the South
events.note: Soviet-planned northern forces take Seoul in three days. Westad argues the war came from Stalin's change of mind: without his go-ahead there would have been none.

events.title: US fleet shields Taiwan
events.note: American warships move into the Taiwan Strait to protect Chiang, frustrating Mao's plan to take the island.

events.title: Security Council creates UN command
events.note: With the Soviets boycotting over China's seat, Truman's resolutions condemning the attack and forming a US-led UN command pass unopposed; Stalin declines to send his envoy back to veto.

events.title: West German economic miracle
events.note: Marshall aid, a mark pegged to the dollar and American relief from war debts and reparations fuel growth above 5 percent a year, making Adenauer's anchoring in the West persuasive.

events.title: Indian peace efforts over Korea
events.note: Nehru condemns Pyongyang's attack yet pushes for a negotiated end; Truman is furious, though Indian diplomacy later helps the truce and prisoner talks.

events.title: Inchon landing
events.note: After holding the Busan perimeter, MacArthur's amphibious assault near Seoul severs northern supply lines and sends Kim's army fleeing north.

events.title: Beijing decides to intervene
events.note: Answering Stalin's appeals, Mao twice overrides a hesitant Politburo and commits troops, though promised Soviet air cover is held back.

events.title: China enters the Korean War
events.note: Some 200,000 Chinese 'volunteers' cross into Korea, rout US troops at Unsan and drive UN forces out of the north by December.

events.title: Chinese troops enter Tibet
events.note: The PLA takes most of Tibet despite covert Indian arms; Nehru urges the Dalai Lama to compromise, while Mao privately brands Nehru an imperialist stooge.

events.title: UN forces invade North Korea
events.note: With Washington's approval, US and allied troops push north and take Pyongyang on 19 October, disregarding Chinese warnings.

events.title: Zhou Enlai meets Stalin
events.note: At Stalin's Black Sea dacha, Zhou bargains over Soviet help for the Chinese intervention; Stalin avoids committing air support early.

events.title: Mao's son killed in Korea
events.note: Westad notes that aircraft of South Africa's squadron carried out the strike that killed Mao Anying, serving as an officer in Korea.

events.title: Apartheid South Africa fights in Korea
events.note: Though it has just passed the Population Registration Act, its first major apartheid law, South Africa sends a fighter squadron to serve under the American-led UN command.

events.title: European Coal and Steel Community founded
events.note: Six states build a supranational market for mining and steel; Westad sees it as a Cold War project driven more by practical need than by idealism.

events.title: Truman fires MacArthur
events.note: After Seoul falls again and MacArthur publicly urges carrying the war into China, Truman dismisses him for defying presidential authority.

events.title: Soviet pilots fly over Korea
events.note: Stalin lets around 800 Soviet pilots fly MiG-15 combat missions within North Korean airspace, as Moscow steps up aid to its allies.

events.title: Iran nationalizes its oil
events.note: Iran's parliament votes to take over the British-run oil industry; London imposes an embargo and seeks American help by warning that the Tudeh Communists will profit.

events.title: Maclean flees to Moscow
events.note: A senior British diplomat unmasked as a Soviet agent escapes to the USSR, part of the Cambridge ring that badly compromised Western intelligence.

events.title: Korean War militarizes the Cold War
events.note: American military spending doubles, NATO turns into an integrated military force, West German rearmament advances and nuclear programs accelerate.

events.title: Korean armistice talks begin
events.note: Talks stall for two years, chiefly over returning prisoners who refuse repatriation; Stalin wants the Americans kept bogged down in Asia.

events.title: Japanese peace and security treaties
events.note: Japan must first accept a bilateral pact making the US its sole ally with free base rights; the Soviets refuse to sign and China is not invited.

events.title: Greece and Turkey join NATO
events.note: Amid the Korean War emergency the Atlantic alliance expands to its south-eastern flank, reinforcing momentum toward wider Western cooperation.

events.title: Árbenz expropriates idle land
events.note: Guatemala hands uncultivated estates, some owned by United Fruit, to a hundred thousand peasant families, with compensation owners call inadequate.

events.title: Free Officers' revolution in Egypt
events.note: Young officers led by Nasser depose King Farouk, preaching anti-imperialism and blaming the old order for the defeat in Palestine.

events.title: Britain becomes a nuclear power
events.note: Britain's first atomic test gives London its own deterrent, which it later refuses to merge into a joint NATO force.

events.title: Eisenhower elected president
events.note: With the war unpopular, Truman stands down; Eisenhower wins promising to end it, then mixes nuclear hints with pressure on Seoul.

events.title: First US hydrogen bomb test
events.note: The US explodes the first thermonuclear device, hundreds of times stronger than the Hiroshima bomb; Moscow matches it within nine months.

events.title: Slánský executed in Prague
events.note: Czechoslovak party chief Rudolf Slánský confesses to absurd espionage charges and is executed; such trials erode faith in Communism in the West.

events.title: Death of Stalin
events.note: Stalin dies after a stroke; his wary successors agree above all on ending the Korean War to signal lower tensions to Washington.

events.title: Churchill urges Eisenhower toward Moscow
events.note: The veteran anti-Communist asks the president to couple firmness with a signal of openness to the post-Stalin leadership; Eisenhower resists summitry for two more years.

events.title: Kremlin frees the accused Jewish doctors
events.note: The first sign of change after Stalin: doctors he had jailed for an alleged murder plot are released, with Beriia branding such cases breaches of socialist legality.

events.title: Beriia arrested and later shot
events.note: Unnerved by the police chief's bold moves, including freeing the Jewish doctors, his Kremlin colleagues conspire to arrest him; he is executed by year's end.

events.title: East German uprising
events.note: Berlin workers' protests over higher output quotas turn into demands for free elections; on 17 June police and Soviet troops crush the revolt, killing at least a hundred.

events.title: Korean armistice signed
events.note: The truce comes three years after the attack, leaving Korea wrecked and divided, with 3.5 million Koreans dead or wounded.

events.title: Soviet 'new course' for eastern Europe
events.note: Moscow urges eased repression, amnesties and more consumer goods; in Hungary Rákosi must share power with Nagy, while most 'little Stalins' resist.

events.title: CIA-backed coup in Iran
events.note: Eisenhower expands CIA covert action and first uses it to bring down an Iranian government he judged a danger to American Cold War aims.

events.title: First Soviet hydrogen bomb test
events.note: Just nine months after the first American thermonuclear device, Moscow tests a comparable weapon, showing it can keep pace in the arms race.

events.title: Khrushchev becomes First Secretary
events.note: Mocked by rivals for his scant schooling and rough manners, the former Ukrainian party boss outplays them all to lead the party.

events.title: Dulles announces massive retaliation
events.note: Dulles lays out deterrence by threat of nuclear strikes where and when Washington chooses; Eisenhower's New Look builds ICBMs and submarine missiles as cheaper than big armies.

events.title: Eisenhower's 'falling domino' remarks
events.note: As the Geneva conference gathers, Eisenhower tells reporters that losing Indochina could topple its neighbors one after another.

events.title: Sino-Indian Panch Sheel agreement
events.note: Talks on Tibet yield Panch Sheel, the Five Principles, which Nehru adopts as a creed for Asian cooperation while conceding Chinese control of Tibet.

events.title: French defeat at Dien Bien Phu
events.note: Viet Minh troops backed by Chinese artillery overwhelm the French; the Paris government falls and Eisenhower refuses to commit US ground forces.

events.title: Guatemala buys Czechoslovak arms
events.note: Árbenz turns to Soviet-bloc Czechoslovakia for weapons; Washington answers with a blockade, though even its allies balk at the American framing of the dispute.

events.title: US-Pakistan military aid agreement
events.note: Eisenhower rewards Pakistan's eager anti-Communism with large-scale arms aid, which Nehru believes is really meant for use against India.

events.title: CIA-backed coup in Guatemala
events.note: A year after Iran, a covert US operation topples Guatemala's government, another regime the president viewed as working against American interests.

events.title: NATO plans nuclear answer to any attack
events.note: Drawing lessons from Korea and conceding Soviet superiority in troops and tanks, NATO's doctrine now foresees using atomic weapons even against a purely conventional Soviet assault on western Europe.

events.title: Gulag releases and 'the Thaw'
events.note: Hundreds of thousands leave the camps as prison labor loses its economic role, though Khrushchev later admits the leaders feared losing control.

events.title: Virgin lands campaign
events.note: Nearly two million people move east to farm the steppe of Kazakhstan and Siberia; early harvests give way to erosion, dust bowls and failure.

events.title: Geneva Conference on Indochina
events.note: Acting in concert, Moscow and Beijing lean on Hanoi's Communists until they agree to a compromise settlement, an example of close alliance diplomacy.

events.title: European Defense Community fails
events.note: The 1950 scheme to place German troops inside a common European army proves too cumbersome and dies when the French parliament, whose government proposed it, refuses to ratify.

events.title: SEATO founded
events.note: Pakistan enters the US-led Southeast Asian pact and later the Baghdad Pact; Nehru denounces both to Dulles in 1956.

events.title: Khrushchev visits Beijing
events.note: Convinced Stalin erred in not embracing the Chinese revolution, Khrushchev makes Beijing his first major trip and greatly expands Soviet economic support.

events.title: Nasser bans the Muslim Brotherhood
events.note: After a Brotherhood member tries to kill him, Nasser outlaws Islamist groups; he jails Communists at times too, but treats the religious Right as his chief domestic foe.

events.title: Algerian War of independence begins
events.note: The FLN starts an armed campaign; France eventually deploys half a million soldiers, paid for largely thanks to US support, yet cannot destroy the movement.

events.title: Senate censures McCarthy
events.note: Once McCarthy attacks the Army, Eisenhower turns against him and the Senate censures him; the hysteria fades but the broad anti-Communist consensus survives.

events.title: Tito visits India
events.note: Tito's lavish praise for Indian foreign policy makes him a hero in Delhi, where he is seen as Asia's friend rather than a colonial envoy.

events.title: Baghdad Pact formed
events.note: Iraq and Turkey launch a Western-backed defence pact that Britain, Pakistan and Iran join; with American support it screens the Soviet south, and monarchist Iraq becomes its hub.

events.title: Khrushchev sidelines Malenkov and Molotov
events.note: Khrushchev strips his chief rival of the premiership, then attacks Molotov, who loses the foreign ministry in 1956; none of the losers is jailed or shot.

events.title: Bandung Afro-Asian Conference
events.note: Sukarno opens a meeting of twenty-nine states whose communiqué stresses sovereignty and non-intervention; he, Nehru and Nasser hope to build a postcolonial alternative to the Cold War.

events.title: Austrian State Treaty
events.note: Moscow's willingness to end the four-power occupation and reunite Austria is one reason Eisenhower finally agrees to a summit.

events.title: Khrushchev apologizes to Tito in Belgrade
events.note: Khrushchev comes in person to mend the 1948 break, blaming Beriia; Tito welcomes him but insists Stalin himself bore the blame.

events.title: Warsaw Pact founded
events.note: Moscow builds a military alliance to counter NATO and expands Comecon, seeking genuine bloc integration with some give and take.

events.title: West Germany joins NATO
events.note: A year after the European army plan dies, the Federal Republic is admitted to NATO as a full member, settling the rearmament question raised by Korea.

events.title: China collectivizes agriculture
events.note: Following terror against larger landowners, China completes the main phase of collectivization in record time, despite peasant reluctance.

events.title: North Vietnamese land reform terror
events.note: A rushed, China-style land campaign leaves about fifteen thousand executed and sends a million fleeing south; even Moscow and Beijing think Hanoi went too far.

events.title: Geneva summit
events.note: The first gathering of the wartime allies' leaders in a decade stays courteous but produces no breakthrough; Eisenhower raises the satellites with Bulganin and is brushed off.

events.title: Military overthrows Perón
events.note: Officers led by Pedro Aramburu drive Perón into a long Spanish exile, while his movement, later including the Montonero guerrillas, agitates for his return.

events.title: Diem founds Republic of Vietnam
events.note: With US backing, the Catholic nationalist Ngo Dinh Diem pushes aside the emperor and makes himself president of a southern state, while promised reforms lag.

events.title: Khrushchev tours India, Burma, Afghanistan
events.note: Implicitly faulting Stalin's neglect of the colonial world, Khrushchev promises Soviet backing and practical cooperation to every state that breaks free of colonialism.

events.title: Japan's Liberal Democratic Party formed
events.note: Uniting Japan's feuding conservatives, the LDP beats the Left and rules for decades, steering investment and exports while Washington opens markets for Japanese goods.

events.title: Khrushchev's secret speech
events.note: At the Twentieth Congress, Khrushchev indicts Stalin's personality cult, terror and wartime blunders, stunning Communists worldwide and shaking their faith.

events.title: Mao airs grievances against Stalin
events.note: Mao tells the Soviet ambassador Stalin distrusted the CCP and treated him like a Chinese Tito, yet fears de-Stalinization could undermine Communist rule.

events.title: India's Second Five Year Plan
events.note: Mahalanobis's blueprint, closer to Soviet planning than to British Labour ideas, drives state-led industrialisation just as India's links with the Soviet bloc grow much warmer.

events.title: Collectivization of Chinese agriculture
events.note: Against Soviet advice to move slowly, Mao drives through collective farming; its apparent success leads him to think still bolder leaps are possible.

events.title: Poznań workers' uprising
events.note: Some 100,000 workers demand lower quotas, cheaper food and free unions; the Polish army under Rokossovsky kills up to a hundred.

events.title: US withdraws Aswan Dam offer
events.note: Suspecting American strings, Nasser turns to Moscow; after Eisenhower angrily cancels the offer, Soviet engineers design and help build the dam, finished in 1970.

events.title: Brioni meeting of Nehru, Nasser, Tito
events.note: Talks on the Yugoslav island launch the idea of formal cooperation among nonaligned states from several continents.

events.title: Nasser nationalizes the Suez Canal
events.note: Frustrated by failed loan talks with Washington, Nasser seizes the canal zone and, invoking the spirit of Bandung, proclaims Arab unity against imperialism.

events.title: Moscow and Beijing rebuke Kim Il-sung
events.note: The two Communist giants jointly discipline the North Korean leader over his purges inside his party, a high point of their cooperation.

events.title: Hungarian revolution
events.note: A Budapest rally inspired by Poland becomes a national uprising; Nagy returns as premier and wins Soviet concessions as revolutionary councils seize local power.

events.title: Polish October
events.note: Reformer Gomułka takes over the party; Khrushchev flies to Warsaw and Soviet units go on alert, but a compromise keeps Poland Communist and allied.

events.title: Suez Crisis
events.note: Israel, Britain and France attack Egypt by prior plan; a furious Eisenhower forces their retreat through oil and currency pressure, showing the old powers can no longer act alone.

events.title: Hungary declares neutrality
events.note: Facing a Soviet invasion, Nagy sides with the revolutionaries, takes the country out of the Soviet alliance and appeals in vain to the UN.

events.title: Soviet invasion of Hungary
events.note: Reversing a pullout decision, Moscow crushes the revolution on 4 November and installs Kádár while the West, distracted by Suez, stands aside; 200,000 Hungarians flee.

events.title: Castro's Granma landing
events.note: Returning from Mexican exile in a battered yacht, Castro's small band reaches Cuba; the few survivors build a guerrilla base in the Sierra Maestra.

events.title: Ghana independence
events.note: Nkrumah leads Ghana to freedom ahead of every other African colony and hopes to steer the liberation of the whole continent.

events.title: Treaty of Rome creates EEC
events.note: Following the Spaak committee's proposals, the six coal and steel partners set up a European Economic Community with a far wider economic remit.

events.title: Hundred Flowers and Anti-Rightist campaign
events.note: Mao briefly invites open criticism; shocked by attacks on bureaucracy, lack of freedom and deference to Moscow, the party reverses course and sends critics to labor camps.

events.title: Khrushchev defeats the 'anti-party group'
events.note: Stalin's old guard tries to topple Khrushchev in the Central Committee and fails; Molotov goes to Mongolia as ambassador, Malenkov and Kaganovich to factories.

events.title: Sputnik launched
events.note: The first artificial satellite thrills Soviet leaders and scares Westerners, who fear space weapons, even as many Soviet citizens still queue for bread.

events.title: Egypt and Syria form United Arab Republic
events.note: Egypt and Syria merge, with backing from some Ba'athists despite the party's suspicion of Nasser; the union ends acrimoniously three years later.

events.title: Algiers revolt brings back de Gaulle
events.note: Rebel officers and settlers in Algiers seize Corsica and demand de Gaulle; he returns pledging to keep Algeria French but cannot turn the war around.

events.title: Great Leap Forward
events.note: Mao's drive to overtake Britain through communes and mass mobilization triggers a famine that kills at least forty million by 1961; Westad ranks it Communism's deadliest campaign.

events.title: Imre Nagy executed
events.note: Nagy is among about 230 people put to death after the revolution; around 20,000 are arrested.

events.title: Soviet development aid to Egypt
events.note: After Suez, Egypt embarks on long-term development with Soviet support, one of several Bandung states turning to Moscow for practical help.

events.title: CIA arms Sumatran rebels against Sukarno
events.note: Alarmed by Sukarno's turn toward the revived PKI, Washington, joined by London and the Dutch, covertly backs Islamic rebels in Sumatra; the operation fails and leaves Sukarno sure the Americans want him gone.

events.title: Iraqi revolution
events.note: Officers massacre the royal family and install Qasim, who allies with Communists and Moscow; Westad calls it a watershed of the regional Cold War.

events.title: Khrushchev's emergency trip to Beijing
events.note: After Mao erupts over Soviet requests for radar and naval radio stations in China, Khrushchev flies in to calm him and receives lectures on American weakness.

events.title: US Marines land in Lebanon
events.note: Eisenhower sends eight thousand marines to Beirut, a show of strength meant to deter Moscow and warn Iraq away from Kuwait.

events.title: Nasser's urgent Moscow visit
events.note: With US Marines ashore in Lebanon, Nasser flies to Moscow; Khrushchev refuses him advanced weapons and offers only a vague pledge of Soviet rockets if Egypt is attacked.

events.title: Second Taiwan Strait crisis
events.note: Weeks after Khrushchev's departure the PLA shells Guomindang-held offshore islands without telling Moscow, signaling to both superpowers that Beijing can act on its own.

events.title: Cuban revolution triumphs
events.note: Batista flees and the rebels enter Havana; Castro decrees land reform and social programs while purging and executing officials of the old regime.

events.title: Khrushchev rebukes China's communes
events.note: At the Soviet party's Twenty-first Congress, Khrushchev warns that no society can leap straight into Communism and that forced egalitarianism discredits it, a pointed rebuff to Mao's Great Leap.

events.title: Hanoi approves armed struggle in south
events.note: Under Le Duan's growing influence the party sanctions a people's war against Diem and starts moving cadres south through Laos along the Ho Chi Minh trail.

events.title: Castro tours the United States
events.note: Greeted like a celebrity, Castro woos American investors and professes friendship, before exile air raids flown from Florida harden his stance by autumn.

events.title: First Americans killed in Vietnam
events.note: Southern Communists kill two US military advisers near Saigon, the first American dead of the new war.

events.title: Delhi ousts Kerala's Communist government
events.note: When Communists win power in Kerala, Nehru has the central government remove them, with Indira Gandhi, then Congress president, brushing aside legal objections.

events.title: Peng Dehuai purged
events.note: When the Korean War marshal voices doubts about the Leap, Mao removes him and presses on, dismissing growing Soviet warnings.

events.title: Sino-Indian border clashes
events.note: Frontier incidents with India enrage Khrushchev, who had spent heavily on winning over Nehru's nonaligned government.

events.title: Khrushchev visits the United States
events.note: The first American tour by a Soviet leader is nearly ignored by the Chinese press, which ramps up anti-American propaganda instead.

events.title: Acrimonious Khrushchev-Mao summit
events.note: Khrushchev's third visit misfires: Chinese leaders take turns attacking him over India and revisionism, he retorts angrily, and the talks break up in bitterness.

events.title: France tests its first nuclear weapon
events.note: The French bomb underlines Paris's determination to keep nuclear independence rather than share command inside NATO.

events.title: Mikoyan's visit opens Soviet-Cuban ties
events.note: The Soviet deputy premier offers loans and trades cheap oil for Cuban sugar, reporting home with delight; Eisenhower launches covert action against Castro the next month.

events.title: Eisenhower launches covert war on Castro
events.note: Weeks after Mikoyan's trip, Eisenhower sets the CIA to train Cuban exiles, sabotage the island's industry and plot Castro's death, leaving Kennedy an invasion plan already in motion.

events.title: Paris summit collapses
events.note: Planned to address Germany and a test ban, the meeting founders when Khrushchev, squeezed by hardliners and Chinese jibes, refuses at the last moment to see Eisenhower.

events.title: U-2 spy plane shot down
events.note: Soviet air defenses down an American reconnaissance flight from Pakistan; Washington's weather-plane cover story collapses when the captured pilot confesses, a propaganda gift to Khrushchev.

events.title: Britain and France dismantle African empires
events.note: After Guinea's 1958 break with Paris, fourteen more French territories win independence by 1962, while Britain's Conservatives, once sworn to keep the empire, free eight countries in the same years.

events.title: Congo independence
events.note: Belgium departs abruptly from a colony with almost no trained Congolese administrators; Lumumba's government faces secession and breakdown within weeks.

events.title: Guatemalan civil wars begin
events.note: The conflicts unleashed by the 1954 intervention fuel civil wars that ravage Guatemala into the 1990s.

events.title: Japanese protests over US security treaty
events.note: Street violence forces Eisenhower to cancel his visit and topples Kishi, but the treaty survives and the LDP pivots to growth shared by all.

events.title: Congo crisis and Soviet appeal
events.note: Lumumba turns to Moscow when UN troops will not hold the country together; Khrushchev pledges help but cannot project power into central Africa, a lesson Soviet officials remember.

events.title: Soviet advisers withdrawn from China
events.note: After open Chinese attacks at Communist meetings, Khrushchev suddenly pulls out most Soviet experts; Mao quietly welcomes the rupture, which Westad says ended the idea of monolithic Communism.

events.title: Army ousts Lumumba
events.note: While a CIA murder plot is still being prepared, Congo's military removes the prime minister, opening the way to a US-backed dictatorship.

events.title: US trade embargo on Cuba
events.note: Tit-for-tat nationalizations and sugar-quota cuts end in an American embargo; Castro seizes all remaining US property and Washington cuts relations in January 1961.

events.title: Ulbricht presses Khrushchev on Berlin
events.note: The East German leader warns Khrushchev that the drain of workers and skilled people into West Berlin is undermining his regime.

events.title: Kennedy defeats Nixon
events.note: Kennedy narrowly beats Eisenhower's vice president after campaigning on an invented missile gap and a promise to outdo the Soviets.

events.title: Japan's income doubling plan
events.note: The promise to double incomes in ten years is met in seven; by 1970 Japan is the world's second-largest economy.

events.title: General rebellion launched in the south
events.note: Westad links Hanoi's timing to the Sino-Soviet split: it plays both patrons, while Moscow, emboldened by Cuba, Algeria and Congo, warms to liberation wars.

events.title: Eisenhower's farewell address
events.note: Having presided over a vast nuclear buildup, the departing president cautions Americans about the growing sway of a permanent arms industry and defense establishment.

events.title: Eisenhower briefs Kennedy on Asia
events.note: At the White House handover the outgoing president warns that Laos is the key to Southeast Asia and that Chinese Communism poses a hard, lasting challenge.

events.title: Kennedy's inaugural address
events.note: The youngest elected president vows that his generation welcomes the task of defending freedom at its most dangerous hour, signalling a more combative Cold War than Eisenhower's.

events.title: Khrushchev backs national liberation
events.note: Addressing the party school, Khrushchev names Asia, Africa and Latin America as the main battlegrounds against imperialism.
