events.title: Lumumba murdered in Katanga
events.note: Handed over to secessionist foes, Lumumba is tortured and killed; Moscow can only protest and name a university after him.

events.title: US breaks diplomatic relations with Cuba
events.note: Days before handing over to Kennedy, Eisenhower cuts diplomatic ties with Havana after Castro answers the embargo by seizing all remaining American property on the island.

events.title: Armed revolt against Portuguese rule
events.note: Liberation fronts in Angola and other Portuguese colonies, and the ANC in South Africa, take up arms, while Johnson worries mainly about Soviet and Chinese influence.

events.title: Alliance for Progress launched
events.note: Kennedy promises to end Latin American poverty within a decade; some programs help, but military aid and counterinsurgency soon overshadow them.

events.title: Bay of Pigs invasion
events.note: Kennedy sends US-trained exiles ashore but withholds air support; the landing is crushed, cementing Castro's rule and pushing him closer to Moscow, JFK's worst mistake bar Vietnam.

events.title: First human in space
events.note: The Soviet space triumph buoys Khrushchev just before he meets Kennedy.

events.title: Castro's movement merges with Communists
events.note: Though marginal in the guerrilla war, Cuban Communists join Castro's organization and hold key posts, while Moscow and Havana argue over armed insurrection.

events.title: Shift to flexible response
events.note: Kennedy and McNamara look beyond massive retaliation, planning conventional defense in Europe first, then tactical nuclear arms, and all-out strikes only as a last resort.

events.title: Laos crisis
events.note: Kennedy treats the Laotian insurgency as a personal test, threatening intervention with fleet moves, alerts and covert operations while avoiding ground troops.

events.title: Vienna summit
events.note: Khrushchev tries to intimidate the young president with a Berlin deadline; Kennedy rejects the ultimatum, then asks Congress for a major military expansion.

events.title: Kennedy's military buildup after Vienna
events.note: Stung by Khrushchev's Berlin ultimatum, Kennedy seeks billions in extra defense spending, new army and marine divisions, a bigger draft and reserve call-ups; Khrushchev answers by ending the test moratorium.

events.title: Berlin Wall erected
events.note: Taking up Ulbricht's idea, Khrushchev seals off East Berlin; Kennedy accepts a wall as better than war, to the disgust of Brandt and de Gaulle.

events.title: Non-Aligned Movement founded in Belgrade
events.note: A wide coalition, including Cuba and Ethiopia but not China, meets in Yugoslavia to defend state sovereignty and peace as a challenge to the bipolar system.

events.title: Syria quits the United Arab Republic
events.note: Syria's secession dissolves the union, one of several setbacks that frustrate Nasser's Soviet-backed regional ambitions.

events.title: Tank standoff at Checkpoint Charlie
events.note: Soviet and American tanks face each other for a day in central Berlin before Washington concludes Moscow will not try to force the West out.

events.title: Stalin removed from the mausoleum
events.note: In the most symbolic gesture of his rule, Khrushchev has Stalin's corpse taken out from beside Lenin and reburied by the Kremlin wall.

events.title: Soviet Tsar Bomba test
events.note: Having ended the testing pause, Khrushchev explodes the biggest bomb ever made, militarily useless but meant to win a contest of nerves.

events.title: Kennedy shifts to flexible response
events.note: Seeking alternatives to all-out retaliation, McNamara's strategy would meet a Soviet attack in Europe first with conventional forces, then tactical nuclear arms, and only finally strikes on Soviet cities.

events.title: Kennedy expands US advisory mission
events.note: Avoiding combat troops, Kennedy raises adviser numbers from six hundred to sixteen thousand, adds air transport, crop-killing herbicides and resettlement villages.

events.title: Mandela trains in Algeria
events.note: Algeria becomes a base for liberation movements, hosting Angola's MPLA, while the ANC leader receives military instruction there.

events.title: Novocherkassk workers' revolt crushed
events.note: Workers demanding food and pay seize party offices and at least thirty are shot, leaving Soviet leaders wary of squeezing labor too hard.

events.title: Kazakh exodus sparks Sino-Soviet border clashes
events.note: As Chinese Kazakhs escape the Great Leap's hunger by crossing into Soviet Kazakhstan, border guards of the two Communist powers clash, an early sign of the frontier hostility to come.

events.title: Cuban-backed revolt in Venezuela fails
events.note: Leftists break from Betancourt and take up arms with Cuban help; their violence costs them support and they are beaten by 1967.

events.title: Algerian independence
events.note: Unable to win and under international pressure, de Gaulle pulls out; the FLN takes power as a radical government intent on symbolizing Third World power.

events.title: Laos neutralized at Geneva
events.note: With Moscow indifferent and a weakened Beijing keen to show cooperation, the powers agree on a neutral Laos under a coalition; Kennedy deepens his South Vietnam commitment.

events.title: Soviet missiles secretly sent to Cuba
events.note: To protect Castro and answer US missiles in Turkey, Khrushchev ships nuclear missiles and tens of thousands of personnel to the island; Castro, consulted late, goes along.

events.title: Egyptian intervention in Yemen
events.note: Over seventy thousand Soviet-supplied Egyptian troops fight royalists backed by the Saudis, Britain and the US; by the late 1960s the costly venture peters out.

events.title: Cuban missile crisis
events.note: After spy planes find the sites, Kennedy imposes a quarantine; a secret deal trading a no-invasion pledge and Turkish missiles ends the standoff, leaving Castro enraged at Moscow.

events.title: Sino-Indian border war
events.note: Fighting in the disputed Himalayas ends in a rout of Indian forces; China gains the territory but, seen as the aggressor, alienates the new nonaligned bloc.

events.title: De Gaulle vetoes British EEC entry
events.note: Seeing Britain as Washington's stalking horse, de Gaulle blocks it, wanting a Europe led by France to balance US power.

events.title: Ba'athist coup in Iraq
events.note: Qasim is toppled and murdered; Ba'athists hostile to Communists gain ground in Baghdad as in Damascus, to Moscow's and Cairo's dismay.

events.title: Pakistan's partnership with China
events.note: Angered by American arms for India in the 1962 war, Pakistan's conservative generals court Beijing, which accepts on enemy-of-my-enemy grounds while Washington remains Islamabad's main ally.

events.title: Buddhist protests against Diem
events.note: Monks burning themselves in Saigon, shown on American TV, expose Diem's clashes with Buddhists, students and his own US patrons.

events.title: Limited Test Ban Treaty
events.note: A modest ban on some nuclear tests shows the superpowers can agree; China, close to its own bomb, sees the pact as directed against it.

events.title: Indonesia's konfrontasi with Malaysia
events.note: Sukarno brands newly independent Malaysia a British neocolonial puppet and wages a three-year, low-level war on it, pitting Indonesian troops against British and Australian forces on Borneo.

events.title: Diem overthrown and killed
events.note: Quietly encouraged by the Kennedy Administration, South Vietnamese generals seize and murder their president; instability only deepens afterward.

events.title: Kennedy assassinated
events.note: Kennedy is killed at forty-six; Westad finds little reason to think he would have ended the Cold War, though Cuba had made him more cautious.

events.title: Zhou Enlai tours Africa
events.note: Competing with Moscow for Third World influence, Zhou offers aid a famine-scarred China can barely afford; by 1965 most of these ties have gone sour.

events.title: Military coup ousts Goulart in Brazil
events.note: Johnson backs the generals against the reformist Goulart; the resulting dictatorship lasts two decades and intensifies Brazil's internal Cold War.

events.title: Death of Nehru
events.note: Broken by the China war, Nehru dies; his successors keep nonalignment but give it a harder, more nationalist regional edge.

events.title: Multilateral nuclear force plan fails
events.note: Washington's idea of a jointly manned sea-based NATO nuclear fleet dies, blocked by British and French insistence on autonomy and unease about German fingers on the trigger.

events.title: Ghana becomes a one-party state
events.note: Losing popularity as his economic plans lag, Nkrumah outlaws rival parties and names himself president for life, two years after dismissing the chief justice.

events.title: Mao raises old Russian land grabs
events.note: Talking to visiting Japanese leftists, Mao says Russia seized the lands east of Lake Baikal a century ago and the account is unsettled, turning the frontier into a weapon against Moscow.

events.title: Gulf of Tonkin resolution
events.note: Using flawed reports of a North Vietnamese attack on a US ship, Johnson wins Congressional authority to widen the war.

events.title: Frei defeats Allende with CIA help
events.note: Allende wins over 38 percent, but the CIA-funded Christian Democrat Frei wins and begins reforms Allende can later build upon.

events.title: China's first nuclear test
events.note: Resting largely on earlier Soviet assistance, the bomb test leaves Mao, once scornful of nuclear arms, feeling far more secure.

events.title: Khrushchev ousted; Brezhnev takes over
events.note: In the first peaceful Soviet leadership change, colleagues remove the erratic Khrushchev, citing his Berlin brinkmanship, and install a collective leadership under Brezhnev.

events.title: US-Belgian airdrop in eastern Congo
events.note: Johnson has US planes fly Belgian paratroopers in to free hostages held by rebels in Kisangani; a CIA-run campaign then helps Tshombe crush the revolt.

events.title: Johnson wins landslide reelection
events.note: Johnson crushes his Republican rival with a record share of the popular vote, riding a major domestic reform program.

events.title: De Gaulle vows to overcome Yalta
events.note: On Yalta's twentieth anniversary de Gaulle pledges to end Europe's division and break the two-superpower game, backed by new ties eastward.

events.title: US bombs North, sends combat troops
events.note: Bombing of the North begins and US troop levels climb toward two hundred thousand; Americans realize this is a real war, not a proxy conflict.

events.title: Che Guevara fights in Congo
events.note: Cuba sends Che with over a hundred fighters to aid the Simba remnants; after seven frustrating months the rebellion collapses by year's end.

events.title: US troops land in Dominican Republic
events.note: Justified as anti-Communist, the invasion fits an older Caribbean pattern that Washington judges impossible to repeat in South America.

events.title: Military deposes Ben Bella
events.note: As his statist economics stumble and his rule turns autocratic, the army removes Ben Bella, to the apparent relief of most Algerians.

events.title: China aids Hanoi, avoids US clash
events.note: Mao urges Hanoi to fight on without talks yet signals Washington he stays out unless the North is invaded; 170,000 Chinese troops serve in Vietnam by 1967.

events.title: Johnson deepens support for Israel
events.note: Seeing Israel as a Western-style anchor, Johnson supplies aid, tanks and bombers and tolerates its nuclear program, leaving Palestinians out of account.

events.title: Kosygin's economic reforms stall
events.note: Premier Kosygin's cautious incentives-based reforms lack backing from planners fearful for their jobs or for ideological purity.

events.title: Second Indo-Pakistani war
events.note: Ayub Khan's disguised push into Kashmir backfires; Shastri strikes at both wings of Pakistan, and neither Washington nor Beijing comes to the rescue.

events.title: Failed coup and army takeover in Jakarta
events.note: A PKI-backed junior officers' plot kills six generals; Suharto's army hits back, takes Jakarta, bans the party and sidelines Sukarno.

events.title: Massacre of Indonesian Communists
events.note: Soldiers and religious militias kill at least half a million, many ethnic Chinese; the US embassy supplies names, and the largest non-bloc Communist party is destroyed.

events.title: Algiers Afro-Asian summit cancelled
events.note: After a wave of overthrown leaders the planned second Bandung never meets; Westad reads it as the start of the Third World project's decline.

events.title: Indira Gandhi becomes prime minister
events.note: Nehru's daughter takes over; tougher than her predecessors and distrustful of the US, she finds the Soviets easier partners against China and Pakistan.

events.title: Soviet-brokered Tashkent settlement
events.note: Moscow plays the rare role of peacemaker; the result is close to the prewar status quo, and Shastri dies during the talks.

events.title: Nkrumah toppled in Ghana
events.note: While Nkrumah travels to China and North Vietnam, officers seize power claiming to block Communism; Washington welcomes the result.

events.title: Radical Ba'athists take Syria
events.note: Moscow backs the new Damascus regime, which hosts Fatah, hoping for a pro-Soviet Ba'athist shift, and ramps up arms to Syria and Egypt.

events.title: France quits NATO military command
events.note: De Gaulle pulls France from the integrated structure; Johnson, sure Paris still wants US troops in Europe, largely shrugs it off.

events.title: Cultural Revolution launched
events.note: Mao turns Red Guards against the party itself; President Liu is beaten and later dies, Deng is sent to a factory, and China slides toward civil war.

events.title: De Gaulle visits Moscow
events.note: Hailed by his hosts after leaving NATO's command, de Gaulle preaches détente and cooperation, though concrete results remain thin.

events.title: Italian Communists chart independent course
events.note: The PCI's program stresses elections and gradual reform; under Berlinguer it keeps Soviet money but eases opposition to NATO, seeding Eurocommunism.

events.title: De Gaulle condemns the US war
events.note: The French president calls the war a Vietnamese national resistance and warns US escalation endangers world peace, reflecting wide European unease.

events.title: Brandt becomes foreign minister
events.note: In the grand coalition Brandt starts bridge-building eastward in small steps, confident his Berlin record shields him from charges of softness.

events.title: Treaty bans mass-destruction weapons in space
events.note: An early sign of détente as leaders resist pressure to arm the satellites both sides were already using for surveillance.

events.title: Martin Luther King denounces the war
events.note: Amid mass protests, the civil rights leader links the war abroad to racial injustice at home and calls his government the leading source of violence.

events.title: Mao lectures North Vietnamese leaders
events.note: Meeting Pham Van Dong and Giap, Mao compares attrition warfare to eating a meal in small bites, typical of the hectoring that drove Hanoi toward Moscow.

events.title: Pyongyang and Hanoi expel Maoist agitators
events.note: Tired of Cultural Revolution propaganda, even China's closest allies arrest and deport Chinese advisers; Pyongyang fumes after students fault Kim Il-sung's grasp of Mao.

events.title: Six-Day War
events.note: Alarmed by Soviet warnings, Nasser blockades Aqaba; Israel strikes first and routs Egypt, Jordan and Syria in under a week, a severe blow to Moscow.

events.title: Soviet aid to Hanoi surges
events.note: Moscow sees a chance to embarrass Washington and chasten Beijing, expanding aid while nudging Hanoi to negotiate when possible.

events.title: Moscow rearms Egypt after defeat
events.note: Blaming Washington for Israel's attack, Brezhnev vows to keep backing the 'progressive' Arabs; Soviet arms and some twenty thousand advisers pour into Egypt, binding Nasser tightly to Moscow.

events.title: Mass protests against the Vietnam War
events.note: Student and activist groups stage huge demonstrations across the United States; many protesters tie the war to racial injustice at home, feeding a sense that the nation is losing its way.

events.title: Red Guards burn British embassy
events.note: Chinese diplomacy disintegrates: ambassadors are recalled for reeducation, the British mission is set alight, and Soviet bloc embassies face round-the-clock mobs.

events.title: De Gaulle visits Poland
events.note: Part of the general's eastern tour promoting détente across the European divide.

events.title: Group of 77 issues Algiers Charter
events.note: Meeting in Algeria, developing states demand fairer commodity prices and more equitable markets as Third World politics turns economic.

events.title: Che Guevara captured and executed
events.note: Che's Bolivian guerrilla fails to win peasants and is hunted down by Barrientos's troops; Westad sees the death of foco theory and populism's strength.

events.title: Nixon urges ending China's isolation
events.note: Before his election Nixon writes that Asia outside Indochina is thriving and a billion Chinese cannot be left permanently outside world society.

events.title: Britain leaves Aden; South Yemen turns Marxist
events.note: Britain pulls out of Aden and the National Liberation Front sets up a people's republic, giving Moscow a doctrinaire Marxist partner in Arabia and naval use of Aden.

events.title: Dubček replaces Novotný as party chief
events.note: Reformers install the Slovak Dubček in place of the aging Novotný, with Brezhnev's approval; he starts with Kosygin-style economic reform but soon faces demands for political openness.

events.title: Tet offensive
events.note: Communist forces strike across the South, even inside the US embassy; a military failure, it convinces many Americans the war cannot be won.

events.title: Johnson declines to seek reelection
events.note: Westad calls it a tragedy: a foreign war waged from Cold War habit wrecks a presidency of great domestic ambition.

events.title: Prague Spring action program
events.note: Installed in January with Brezhnev's approval, Dubček ends censorship and promises socialism with a human face; talk of leaving the Warsaw Pact alarms Moscow.

events.title: De Gaulle visits Romania
events.note: The Romanian regime gives the French leader a hero's welcome for his challenge to bloc politics.

events.title: May 1968 revolt in France
events.note: Student protests spread to a mass strike and de Gaulle briefly flees to his troops in Germany; Westad sees the Communists as the real losers.

events.title: Hanoi opens talks with Washington
events.note: After Tet, Hanoi accepts tentative talks; Zhou berates its negotiator for weakness, pushing Le Duan closer to Moscow.

events.title: Gaullists win snap election
events.note: Voters endorse the established order and the Communists lose half their seats.

events.title: Soviet-Czechoslovak border summit
events.note: Brezhnev demands an end to anti-Soviet commentary and Dubček promises to comply; Moscow holds off on invading, for now.

events.title: EEC completes its customs union
events.note: Internal tariffs among the six are gone a decade after Rome; West German industry gains free access in return for funding French and Italian farm subsidies.

events.title: Brezhnev's final call to Dubček
events.note: Brezhnev accuses Dubček of deceit over the press and threatens independent measures; days later the tanks roll.

events.title: Warsaw Pact invades Czechoslovakia
events.note: Soviet, Polish, Hungarian and Bulgarian troops occupy the country; Dubček is taken to Moscow to sign away reforms, while Johnson barely reacts.

events.title: Ceaușescu condemns the invasion
events.note: To Brezhnev's dismay a Warsaw Pact member calls the invasion a grave error; most West European Communist parties, led by the PCI, also object.

events.title: Brezhnev doctrine proclaimed
events.note: Addressing the Poles, Brezhnev asserts that any socialist state drifting toward capitalism is the business of every socialist country.

events.title: Nixon elected president
events.note: After a year of assassinations and unrest, Nixon narrowly wins a three-way race by courting a silent majority and promising honorable peace in Vietnam.

events.title: Sino-Soviet border clashes
events.note: A Chinese ambush on a disputed Ussuri River island kills dozens of Soviet guards; counterattacks and shelling follow, and some in Moscow urge strikes on Chinese nuclear sites.

events.title: War of Attrition
events.note: Egypt, with Syria and Soviet backing, keeps up limited raids on Israeli lines; Golda Meir hits back harder and will not give up occupied land.

events.title: De Gaulle resigns after referendum defeat
events.note: His exit relieves defenders of the European status quo and opens the door to British entry into the Common Market.

events.title: Husák replaces Dubček
events.note: Once Dubček has served as a compromised figurehead, Moscow's chosen successor Gustáv Husák takes over and makes Czechoslovakia the harshest regime of the Soviet camp.

events.title: Chinese marshals' strategic review
events.note: Recalled from disgrace, four veteran commanders judge the USSR the greater danger, hinting that easing tensions with Washington would help against Moscow.

events.title: Apollo moon landing
events.note: American astronauts reach the moon; afterward Nixon and Brezhnev start to see joint space work as a potent emblem of détente, leading to a cooperation pact in 1972.

events.title: Nixon doctrine for Asia
events.note: Nixon tells Saigon's Thieu that America will still back anti-Communist Asian governments but will no longer send its own troops to fight for them.

events.title: Nixon visits Pakistan and Romania
events.note: The first US president in a Communist country, Nixon asks his hosts in Bucharest and Pakistan to tell Mao and Zhou he wants talks.

events.title: Brandt becomes West German chancellor
events.note: The first Social Democratic head of government since 1930 launches Ostpolitik, seeking change through rapprochement with the East.

events.title: Chinese war scare and evacuation
events.note: Fearing Soviet nuclear attack, Mao orders the leadership out of Beijing even as Zhou talks with the Soviet premier; the scare pushes him to rein in radicals.

events.title: Strategic arms talks begin
events.note: Brezhnev wants stability but refuses to be hurried, believing time favors Moscow; an impatient Nixon presses Kissinger for any deal.

events.title: Sihanouk ousted, finds refuge in Beijing
events.note: Cambodia's king is deposed while abroad and exiled in Beijing, where Mao hosts him; within weeks US forces push into Cambodia to cut Hanoi's supply lines.

events.title: Soviet air-defence deployment in Egypt
events.note: Soviet crews in civilian disguise man missile sites and fly missions near the canal; the August ceasefire leaves the missiles in place.

events.title: US offensive into Cambodia
events.note: Aimed at Hanoi's supply lines, the attacks convince Beijing that Nixon is laying a trap; Mao denounces them and hosts Sihanouk.

events.title: Montoneros kill ex-dictator Aramburu
events.note: Peronist urban guerrillas win brief popularity, then lose it in a relentless campaign of bombings, kidnappings and murders.

events.title: West German-Soviet Moscow Treaty
events.note: Brandt accepts postwar borders as inviolable in return for trade; Brezhnev dismisses Bonn's reunification caveat, sure Germany needs Moscow more.

events.title: Allende wins Chilean presidency
events.note: Despite CIA efforts, the Popular Unity candidate wins and pledges a lawful, peaceful transition to socialism that splits Chilean society.

events.title: Black September in Jordan
events.note: After spectacular PFLP hijackings, King Hussein expels the PLO from Jordan despite Syrian threats, splitting Arab ranks and embarrassing Moscow.

events.title: Death of Nasser
events.note: Nasser's sudden death brings Anwar Sadat to power, torn between squeezing Moscow for arms and eventually bargaining with Washington.

events.title: Nixon orders pressure on Allende
events.note: Nixon and Kissinger fear a democratic Marxist model worse than Cuba; the CIA funds the opposition and Washington squeezes Chile's economy.

events.title: Polish workers protest price rises
events.note: Mass protests against higher prices frighten Poland's rulers, who with Moscow's consent borrow heavily from Western lenders to buy calm, about $20 billion by 1977.

events.title: Warsaw Treaty and Brandt's kneeling
events.note: Bonn confirms Poland's western frontier; kneeling in silence at the ghetto memorial, Brandt projects a new Germany more powerfully than any treaty.

events.title: Pakistani crackdown in East Pakistan
events.note: After the Awami League's election win is annulled, the army assaults Bengali districts; millions flee to India and Gandhi speaks of genocide.

events.title: Indira Gandhi's landslide victory
events.note: After nationalising banks and splitting Congress in 1969, Gandhi's faction sweeps the polls on an anti-poverty slogan and pushes India toward tighter central planning.

events.title: Mao invites Nixon to Beijing
events.note: After two years of hesitation Mao answers Nixon's feelers, sending an offer of top-level talks through Pakistan; Nixon, frustrated by Soviet stalling on arms control, accepts at once.

events.title: Soviet-Egyptian friendship treaty
events.note: Sadat signs a defence treaty with Moscow, crowning years of massive Soviet military aid and advisers.

events.title: Ceaușescu meets Mao in Beijing
events.note: Asked by the Romanian go-between whether China might mend ties with Moscow, Mao vows to keep up the quarrel for ten thousand years.

events.title: Kissinger's secret mission to Beijing
events.note: Faking illness in Pakistan, Kissinger flies to Beijing, where Zhou insists Washington must accept the PRC as China's only government and drop Taiwan.

events.title: Nixon announces trip to China
events.note: The televised surprise stuns the world; Japan's premier Sato, told minutes beforehand, feels betrayed by his American ally.

events.title: Nixon ends dollar-gold convertibility
events.note: Suspending gold convertibility devalues the dollar and wrecks Bretton Woods; Westad sees Washington putting its own interests first as capitalism globalizes.

events.title: Indo-Soviet friendship treaty
events.note: Told the US would not help against a Chinese intervention, Gandhi accepts Moscow's offer of a treaty with consultation clauses, surprising Washington and Beijing.

events.title: Lin Biao's flight and death
events.note: Mao's chosen heir, sure he is about to be purged, flees toward the USSR and dies in a crash in Mongolia; popular faith in the Cultural Revolution turns to cynicism.

events.title: Bangladesh liberation war
events.note: India's rapid offensive creates Bangladesh; Nixon and Kissinger dispatch naval forces and vow to punish Delhi, which emerges dominant and closer to Moscow.

events.title: Nixon in Beijing
events.note: An ailing Mao briefly receives Nixon and says he prefers rightists; Nixon pitches cooperation against Moscow to Zhou. Westad calls it a strategic earthquake for Asia.

events.title: Shanghai Communiqué
events.note: Both sides state positions separately, agree to work toward normalization, and Washington accepts one China while promising to reduce forces on Taiwan.

events.title: Soviet-Iraqi friendship treaty
events.note: Ba'athist Iraq, soon dominated by Saddam Hussein, binds itself to Moscow with an April 1972 treaty and comes to lean on Soviet and East European help for security and development.

events.title: Moscow summit and SALT I
events.note: Spurred by the China opening, Brezhnev completes SALT I and Basic Principles that treat the USSR as an equal; he counts it his statesmanship peak.

events.title: Sadat expels Soviet advisers
events.note: Irked that Moscow withholds longer-range missiles, Sadat sends many Soviet advisers home and secretly reaches out to the Americans.

events.title: Munich Olympics attack
events.note: Palestinian gunmen kill Israeli athletes; Arafat's refusal to condemn such violence publicises the cause but costs it sympathy.

events.title: Japan and China establish relations
events.note: Sato's successor Tanaka hurries to Beijing; the two recognize Taiwan as Chinese territory and jointly oppose regional hegemony, meaning Moscow.

events.title: Nixon reelected
events.note: Nixon wins a second term, but the Watergate scandal soon consumes his presidency.

events.title: Brandt reelected with strong mandate
events.note: Voters endorse Brandt, though he is unsure where to take Ostpolitik next.

events.title: Basic Treaty between two German states
events.note: After years of refusing talks without recognition, East Berlin deals directly with Bonn; each accepts the other's jurisdiction, a first step toward rapprochement.

events.title: Paris Peace Accords on Vietnam
events.note: A patchwork deal affirms both Vietnamese unity and southern sovereignty; Nixon forces Saigon to sign, and Mao advises Hanoi to pause before conquering the South.

events.title: Britain joins the European Community
events.note: With de Gaulle gone, London joins alongside Denmark, making the common market look like NATO's economic arm and reassuring Washington.

events.title: European security conference talks open
events.note: Moscow wanted a propaganda forum but, with US participation required, is drawn in and surprisingly accepts human rights as Basket III.

events.title: Pinochet's coup overthrows Allende
events.note: Newly named army chief Pinochet turns on his president; Allende dies as troops storm the palace, and thousands are killed or tortured.

events.title: Both Germanys join the UN
events.note: At the UN Brandt calls for everyday peace, cuts in arms budgets and an end to the Cold War without winners or losers.

events.title: Arab oil embargo
events.note: Arab producers, even Saudi Arabia, cut off Israel's backers; oil prices double, battering Western economies and encouraging Third World economic demands.

events.title: Perón returns as Argentine president
events.note: The exiled populist comes back to power, yet guerrilla violence continues and the country seems ungovernable by 1975.

events.title: US DEFCON 3 alert
events.note: Brezhnev threatens intervention; a Watergate-weakened Nixon puts forces on global alert while Kissinger restrains Israel, exposing the limits of détente.

events.title: Yom Kippur (October) War
events.note: Egypt and Syria attack by surprise; Israel readies nuclear forces, rival US and Soviet airlifts follow, and an Israeli counteroffensive encircles an Egyptian army.

events.title: Kissinger's disengagement deals
events.note: Kissinger brokers separation-of-forces accords, but Golda Meir's government blocks any wider bargain over occupied land.

events.title: Solzhenitsyn expelled from USSR
events.note: The exile of the camp chronicler, followed by Amalrik's, links Soviet dissent with a growing Western focus on individual liberties.

events.title: Carnation Revolution in Portugal
events.note: Junior officers, worn down by colonial wars and the oil shock, topple the dictatorship without bloodshed and promise the colonies independence.

events.title: Brandt resigns over East German spy
events.note: An aide is exposed as a GDR agent; fearing blackmail, Brandt quits and the more skeptical Helmut Schmidt continues Ostpolitik.

events.title: India's first nuclear test
events.note: Soviet assistance aids India's self-described peaceful nuclear explosion, at the high point of mid-1970s Soviet-Indian cooperation.

events.title: UN adopts New International Economic Order
events.note: The Group of 77 wins a vote for resource cartels, controls on multinationals and debt relief; Washington condemns it as majority tyranny.

events.title: Nixon resigns over Watergate
events.note: Facing impeachment for obstructing the break-in inquiry, Nixon becomes the first president to resign; Ford keeps détente going with Kissinger at State.

events.title: Ethiopian revolution
events.note: Young officers of the Dergue depose Haile Selassie; Mengistu takes charge and courts Moscow and Havana, at first to little Soviet enthusiasm.

events.title: Brezhnev meets Ford
events.note: Brezhnev, haunted by wartime devastation, tells the new US president he never wants his people to suffer war again.

events.title: Jackson-Vanik amendment
events.note: Senator Jackson's drive ties Soviet trade status to human rights and emigration, enraging Moscow and signalling the domestic revolt against détente.

events.title: EEC signs Lomé Convention
events.note: Nudged by Brandt and others, the Community grants former colonies duty-free access and billions in aid, one modest fruit of Southern demands.

events.title: Ford orders reassessment of Israel ties
events.note: Angered by Rabin's rejection of an interim deal with Egypt, Ford threatens a policy review, but 76 senators push back and he retreats.

events.title: Fall of Saigon
events.note: Hanoi's all-out offensive, fuelled by Soviet supplies, overruns the South within weeks; the helicopter evacuation marks the low point of postwar US policy.

events.title: Khmer Rouge seize Cambodia
events.note: Pol Pot's regime empties the cities and turns on minorities; roughly a third of Cambodians die under its rule.

events.title: Chile's neoliberal economic experiment
events.note: Pinochet hands policy to free-market economists trained in Chicago, impoverishing workers but positioning Chile early for the global neoliberal turn.

events.title: Indira Gandhi's Emergency rule
events.note: Facing a court ruling against her, Gandhi suspends liberties and governs by decree; Moscow hopes India may drift toward one-party socialism.

events.title: Apollo-Soyuz space docking
events.note: Growing out of the 1972 space accord, the linkup of American and Soviet crews in orbit becomes a vivid image of détente.

events.title: Helsinki Final Act signed
events.note: Thirty-five states endorse fixed borders and nonintervention, Brezhnev's career peak, but also human rights clauses whose later impact nobody foresaw.

events.title: Angolan independence
events.note: As Portugal withdraws, the MPLA proclaims a People's Republic in the middle of a civil war with the FNLA and UNITA.

events.title: Brazil recognizes Marxist Angola
events.note: Brazil's generals pursue a Thirdworldist line, backing the Luanda government Washington opposes; the US drops military cooperation in 1977.

events.title: Cuban intervention in Angola
events.note: Cuban troops with Soviet arms repel a South African advance backed covertly by Washington; Moscow follows Havana's lead and treats it as payback.

events.title: Congress halts covert aid in Angola
events.note: Over White House protests, Congress bans further military help to the MPLA's Angolan rivals, and the retreating South Africans feel let down by Washington.

events.title: Argentine junta seizes power
events.note: Generals under Videla depose Isabel Perón and murder thousands, mostly unionists, students and journalists, trusting Washington not to cut ties.

events.title: Soares's Socialists win in Portugal
events.note: An odd alliance of Eurocommunists, Social Democrats, Catholics and the CIA helps non-Communists; Soares's victory brings relief in Europe and Washington.

events.title: Vietnam reunified as socialist republic
events.note: Northern leaders impose Soviet-style socialism on the South; re-education camps and economic collapse drive two million Vietnamese abroad.

events.title: Reagan challenges Ford for nomination
events.note: Reagan assails détente and Kissinger, claiming America has sunk to second place; Ford keeps the nomination but emerges damaged.

events.title: Death of Mao
events.note: Mao's death lets Deng return from political disgrace; within two years the radical Maoist leaders, Jiang Qing among them, are under arrest.

events.title: Carter defeats Ford
events.note: Carter, promising values over power politics, narrowly beats a Ford who had even dropped the word détente from his campaign.

events.title: Charter 77 manifesto
events.note: Czechoslovak dissidents including Havel denounce censorship and repression; the regime jails rock musicians and later sentences Havel to four years.

events.title: Carter's letter to Sakharov
events.note: Carter's public human-rights message to the dissident physicist infuriates the Kremlin, which freezes plans for an early summit.

events.title: Moscow starts arming Mengistu's Ethiopia
events.note: Setting aside doubts about the Dergue's Marxism and worries for its Somali alliance, Moscow begins supplying Mengistu with weapons and military training while Cuba sends advisers.

events.title: Indira Gandhi loses election
events.note: Sure of victory, Gandhi calls a vote and loses to Morarji Desai's coalition, which restores democracy but keeps the Soviet partnership intact.

events.title: Likud wins Israeli election
events.note: Labor loses power for the first time; Menachem Begin seeks peace with neighbours but not at the price of the West Bank.

events.title: Soviets deploy SS-20 missiles
events.note: Brezhnev fields mobile medium-range SS-20s to replace poor older missiles; though no treaty forbids it, West European leaders read the move as intimidation and push NATO to respond.

events.title: Ogaden War
events.note: Somalia invades Ethiopia; Moscow switches sides, airlifts arms and backs Cuban troops, and Washington reads it as proof of Soviet expansionism.

events.title: Berlinguer's Eurocommunist challenge in Moscow
events.note: In Moscow the Italian Communist leader calls democracy a universal value, shocking Brezhnev, who keeps funding Western parties for fear of losing them.

events.title: Sadat's visit to Jerusalem
events.note: Sadat travels to Israel for direct talks with Begin, making Egypt an Arab outcast but securing US mediation.

events.title: Carter cancels neutron bomb
events.note: After West European leaders defy public opinion to accept the weapon, Carter drops it unilaterally, infuriating Helmut Schmidt.

events.title: Communist coup in Afghanistan
events.note: Afghan Marxists seize power and force radical reforms against Soviet advice, provoking an Islamist revolt organised from Pakistan and Iran.

events.title: Red Brigades murder Aldo Moro
events.note: The killing of a former Italian premier, a year after Baader-Meinhof murdered Schleyer, shakes Europe; the Stasi quietly aids West German terrorists.

events.title: Sino-Vietnamese split turns military
events.note: Relations between Hanoi and Beijing, souring since 1975, collapse into insults and border troop build-ups; Deng reads Vietnam's closer Soviet ties as a plan to encircle China.

events.title: Camp David accords
events.note: A US-brokered separate peace returns Sinai to Egypt; after the March 1979 treaty Cairo receives a surge of American aid.

events.title: Polish pope elected
events.note: Kraków's archbishop Karol Wojtyła becomes John Paul II, giving Poland's devout workers a powerful new inspiration.

events.title: Deng's market reforms begin
events.note: Deng dismantles the communes, lets farmers and firms sell surpluses and opens special zones to foreign capital, breaking decisively with socialist planning.

events.title: Vietnam invades Cambodia
events.note: After Khmer Rouge border raids, Vietnam's far larger army topples Pol Pot within two weeks and installs a friendly regime.

events.title: Deng Xiaoping visits Washington
events.note: Deng tells Carter that China will teach Vietnam a limited lesson and sees no chance of détente with Moscow.

events.title: US-China diplomatic normalisation
events.note: After Ethiopia, Washington speeds full recognition of Beijing; Deng wants American technology and trade and fears Soviet encirclement.

events.title: Iranian revolution
events.note: The Shah flees and Khomeini returns to lead an Islamic republic hostile to both superpowers, sending oil prices soaring again.

events.title: China attacks Vietnam
events.note: China's month-long punitive war costs it heavy losses; Carter publicly deplores it but secretly passes intelligence to Beijing.

events.title: Thatcher becomes prime minister
events.note: A free-market ideologue takes office, backing a common market but resisting political union to protect the US special relationship.

events.title: Desai meets Brezhnev in Moscow
events.note: The two aging leaders reaffirm their partnership and share confusion and alarm over Iran's Islamist upheaval.

events.title: John Paul II visits Poland
events.note: Over a quarter of all Poles see the pope in person; vast crowds chant for God as he calls for the nation's spiritual renewal.

events.title: Rawlings seizes power in Ghana
events.note: A young air force officer takes over Ghana, one of many military regimes spreading across Africa as the decade turns.

events.title: Vienna summit and SALT II
events.note: The first summit in nearly five years goes badly; the treaty is signed amid mutual complaints, and the Senate stalls ratification.

events.title: Sandinista revolution in Nicaragua
events.note: Marxist-inspired rebels oust a US-backed dictator and launch radical reforms; Castro counsels them not to provoke Washington too quickly.

events.title: US begins aiding Afghan Islamists
events.note: Even before Soviet troops arrive, Washington starts helping the Afghan Islamist insurgents, whose revolt against the Communist regime is organised from Pakistan and Iran.

events.title: Amin kills Taraki
events.note: Taraki's deputy Amin takes over; the KGB suspects him of American contacts, and Moscow prepares to remove him.

events.title: Havel jailed for four years
events.note: Prague sentences the playwright and Charter 77 figure Václav Havel to prison, part of a crackdown that also sweeps up underground rock musicians.

events.title: Iran hostage crisis
events.note: Khomeini backs militants holding US diplomats in Tehran, blocking reconciliation; the standoff wrecks Carter's presidency.

events.title: Lancaster House Agreement on Rhodesia
events.note: London and Washington, helped by Botha, push white Rhodesia into majority rule; Zimbabwe emerges in 1980 under Mugabe, who keeps Moscow at a distance.

events.title: NATO double-track decision
events.note: Answering Soviet SS-20s, NATO plans Pershing II and cruise missile deployments while offering arms talks; Schmidt is its chief architect.

events.title: Soviet invasion of Afghanistan
events.note: Soviet troops move in on Christmas Eve to replace Amin; Carter sees proof of a Soviet drive through an arc of crisis toward Gulf oil.

events.title: Carter's sanctions and doctrine
events.note: Carter calls the invasion the gravest threat since 1945, embargoes grain, threatens an Olympic boycott, shelves SALT II and lifts defence spending.

events.title: US grain embargo on the USSR
events.note: Carter halts grain sales to punish the Afghan invasion; Reagan lifts the ban a year later because it hurt US farmers, but East-West trade is already damaged.

events.title: Indira Gandhi returns to power
events.note: Back in office, Gandhi fears that religious and ethnic mobilisation, from Iran to Afghanistan, threatens India's unity and her hopes for détente.

events.title: Sakharov banished to Gorky
events.note: Nobel laureate Andrei Sakharov, a founder of the Moscow Helsinki monitoring group, is sent into internal exile in Gorky, watched closely and kept from foreign reporters.

events.title: Failed hostage rescue mission
events.note: The rescue attempt collapses in the desert after an aircraft collision, prompting Vance's resignation.

events.title: Schmidt meets Brezhnev in Moscow
events.note: Defying Washington, Schmidt tells Brezhnev the Afghan invasion was a grave error but wins Soviet readiness to discuss nuclear arms in Europe.

events.title: Gdansk strike and Solidarity's birth
events.note: Wałęsa leads a shipyard occupation; the regime concedes an independent union in televised talks, and Solidarity soon claims about ten million members.

events.title: Iran-Iraq War
events.note: Iraq's land grab against Iran turns into a Sunni-Shia slaughter costing nearly a million lives; Westad calls it an early post-ideological war neither superpower welcomed.

events.title: Reagan defeats Carter
events.note: Reagan routs Carter, blaming him for inflation, oil shocks and Soviet gains, and vows to end détente and restore American greatness.

events.title: Greece joins European Community
events.note: A fast-tracked accession Westad reads as a Cold War bargain: aid for southern Europe in return for giving up revolutionary alternatives.

events.title: Mitterrand elected French president
events.note: The Socialist brings Communists into his cabinet, dismaying Washington, before a sharp turn toward fiscal prudence.

events.title: Reagan arms Zia's Pakistan
events.note: Zia, who had Bhutto hanged and rules through conservative clerics, convinces Reagan that Moscow aims to crush Pakistan; generous US military aid follows, and Pakistan becomes the mujahedin's supply route.

events.title: US backs the Contras
events.note: Reagan's administration arms and trains counterrevolutionaries, first to halt Sandinista aid to Salvadoran rebels, then to overthrow the government.

events.title: Martial law in Poland
events.note: Jaruzelski arrests thousands of Solidarity activists; Moscow urged the crackdown but, as Andropov insisted, would not send troops if it failed.

events.title: Reagan's gas pipeline sanctions
events.note: Reagan penalises firms, European ones included, that help build Siberian gas pipelines; he later relents, but transatlantic unity suffers.

events.title: Syrian regime crushes Islamist revolt
events.note: Assad's Ba'athist government smashes an Islamist rising in western Syria, reportedly even with chemical weapons; at least ten thousand people are killed.

events.title: Falklands War
events.note: Thatcher rebuffs Reagan's plea for mediation and retakes the islands from Argentina's junta, boosting her standing.

events.title: Reagan expands aid to mujahedin
events.note: Washington steps up support for Afghan Islamists and their Pakistani sponsors to bleed the Soviets, despite the rebels' own anti-Americanism.

events.title: Indira Gandhi meets Reagan
events.note: Gandhi assures Reagan India wants good relations with America and a Soviet exit from Afghanistan, but US arms for Pakistan limit the thaw.

events.title: Latin American debt crisis
events.note: Soaring US interest rates trigger Mexico's default; IMF structural adjustment imposes neoliberal cures, bringing a lost decade and hastening the juntas' demise.

events.title: Kohl replaces Schmidt
events.note: The new conservative chancellor keeps paying East Berlin for contacts and emigrants, convinced that some contact beats none.

events.title: Death of Brezhnev
events.note: Brezhnev leaves a military superpower but a stagnant system; the former KGB chief Andropov succeeds him.

events.title: Reagan's 'focus of evil' speech
events.note: Rhetoric peaks as Reagan casts the USSR as the centre of evil and Soviet leaders compare him to Hitler.

events.title: Mitterrand's turn to austerity
events.note: With the economy faltering, Mitterrand abandons nationalisation plans and later his Communist ministers, anchoring a market model in the EC.

events.title: Reagan launches SDI
events.note: Repelled by mutual assured destruction, Reagan orders a space-based missile shield; Moscow is alarmed because it cannot match the technology.

events.title: Argentina's military junta falls
events.note: Discredited by its failed Falklands grab, the regime that committed vast abuses while claiming to fight Communism gives way to civilian rule, part of a wider Latin American retreat from dictatorship.

events.title: Stuttgart Declaration on European union
events.note: EC leaders pledge to build a united Europe; Thatcher backs the single market but distrusts deeper political integration.

events.title: Soviets shoot down Korean airliner
events.note: A Soviet fighter downs a straying Korean jet, killing 269; Moscow's initial denials hand Reagan a propaganda windfall.

events.title: Mass protests against NATO missiles
events.note: Over three million West Europeans rally against new missiles; the END campaign also targets Soviet SS-20s and links up with Eastern dissidents.

events.title: Able Archer war scare
events.note: A NATO nuclear-release exercise prompts heightened Soviet alert; Westad judges accidental war nearer than for years, and the episode sobers Reagan.

events.title: Reagan's appeal to the Soviet people
events.note: Shaken by Able Archer and a TV drama about nuclear war, Reagan tells Soviet citizens atomic war is unwinnable and floats scrapping such weapons altogether.

events.title: Death of Andropov
events.note: The ailing Andropov dies after barely a year; the sickly Chernenko, a Brezhnev crony, follows and dies within about a year.

events.title: CIA mines Nicaraguan harbors
events.note: The CIA covertly mines Nicaragua's ports; a wary Congress responds with the Boland amendment forbidding US support for the Contras' war.

events.title: Deng meets Nakasone
events.note: Deng extols lasting Sino-Japanese friendship; by 1987 Japan is China's top trading partner and a vital source of loans and technology.

events.title: Boland amendment bars Contra aid
events.note: Fearing another Vietnam, Congress forbids any US backing for armed action in Nicaragua, blocking Reagan's widening aim of toppling the Sandinistas and pushing the White House toward covert funding.

events.title: Indira Gandhi assassinated
events.note: Her son Rajiv takes over and turns to Gorbachev as a fellow reformer who puts economic development ahead of ideology.

events.title: Gorbachev becomes Soviet leader
events.note: When Chernenko dies, Gromyko proposes the 54-year-old Gorbachev, the youngest Politburo member; nobody foresees how far the new general secretary will go.

events.title: Anti-alcohol and anticorruption drives
events.note: Gorbachev's first measures borrow from Andropov: campaigns against graft and drinking that do little for output and a lot for jokes at his expense.

events.title: Reagan's offensive against the Third World Left
events.note: Washington arms insurgents against Soviet-aligned governments in Angola and Cambodia to raise the price of Moscow's commitments, turning 1970s Soviet methods back on it, Westad argues.

events.title: Reagan arms Savimbi's UNITA
events.note: CIA money, training and, in 1986, Stinger missiles go to UNITA, which Reagan treats as a lever to force Cubans and Soviets out of Africa.

events.title: US arms Afghan mujahedin via Pakistan
events.note: Encouraged by Zia, Reagan expands CIA supplies through Pakistan, favouring Islamist parties as the most effective killers of Soviet troops.

events.title: US and China back Cambodian resistance
events.note: To punish Vietnam's Soviet alliance, Washington and Beijing sustain the anti-Hanoi guerrillas, Khmer Rouge remnants included; Westad calls it a perverse partnership.

events.title: Shevardnadze replaces Gromyko
events.note: Gorbachev moves the veteran Gromyko to the ceremonial presidency and gives foreign affairs to Georgia's reform-minded party chief, who becomes his closest partner in remaking Soviet diplomacy.

events.title: Geneva summit
events.note: First top-level superpower meeting in six years produces little of substance but lets the two leaders size each other up; Reagan concludes he can do business personally.

events.title: Spain and Portugal join EC
events.note: Southern enlargement brings rapid gains, offering East Europeans a tempting picture of a Europe beyond blocs.

events.title: 27th CPSU Congress
events.note: Gorbachev admits economic and moral failings in an unusually frank report, strengthens his own position and commits himself firmly to reform.

events.title: Chernobyl nuclear disaster
events.note: A reactor explosion followed by days of official silence exposes Soviet secrecy and environmental neglect; Gorbachev later cites it to justify glasnost.

events.title: Gorbachev urges Honecker to reform
events.note: Gorbachev tells the East German leader to follow his own course but widen his regime's support; the relationship soon turns sour.

events.title: Oil price collapse
events.note: Oil prices fall by about two-thirds, cutting the hard-currency earnings the Soviet economy depends on just as reform needs resources.

events.title: Gorbachev resolves to quit Afghanistan
events.note: A year of harsher offensives fails and US-supplied Stinger missiles make air operations costly, so Gorbachev tells the Politburo the army must get out.

events.title: US gives mujahedin Stinger missiles
events.note: Washington hands the Afghan Islamists shoulder-fired anti-aircraft missiles, a step that startles even London; Soviet air power loses its edge and Gorbachev's harder military push stalls.

events.title: Serbian Academy memorandum
events.note: Leading Serbian intellectuals claim their nation is held down inside Yugoslavia, an early sign of the identity politics that would soon pull the federation apart.

events.title: Reykjavik summit
events.note: The leaders come close to agreeing to abolish nuclear arsenals, but the deal founders on SDI; Westad says it nonetheless opened unmapped possibilities.

events.title: Congress imposes South Africa sanctions
events.note: Lawmakers impose broad sanctions on the apartheid state over Reagan's objections, adding pressure for a southern African settlement.

events.title: Delhi Declaration
events.note: Gorbachev and Rajiv Gandhi sign principles on nonviolence and new thinking that, in Westad's reading, bear a stronger Indian imprint than a Soviet one.

events.title: Iran-Contra scandal breaks
events.note: Once the scandal surfaces, Reagan cannot keep financing his Central American campaign without an open clash with Congress.

events.title: Vietnam's Doi Moi reforms
events.note: Ahead of real change in Moscow, Hanoi brings market principles into much of its economy, learning from Chinese experiments and even more from ASEAN neighbours.

events.title: Perestroika and glasnost launched
events.note: At a Central Committee plenum Gorbachev demands a basic restructuring; enterprise autonomy and limited private business follow, while eased censorship unleashes scrutiny of Soviet crimes.

events.title: Rust lands on Red Square
events.note: A young West German flies a light plane unchallenged to Moscow; Gorbachev seizes on the humiliation to retire much of the high command.

events.title: South Korea turns democratic
events.note: As regional tension eases, Seoul's regime opens the way to democracy; Taiwan follows in 1991, and both become very wealthy.

events.title: Reagan's Brandenburg Gate speech
events.note: Reagan publicly dares Gorbachev to open the Berlin Wall; Gorbachev bristles at US meddling, though an aide senses he expects German unity eventually.

events.title: Single European Act takes effect
events.note: The boldest EC integration step in three decades binds members to a borderless single market and eventual union, calming fears of German dominance and pointing toward Maastricht.

events.title: Arias peace plan for Central America
events.note: A Costa Rican plan becomes the basis for ending the isthmus's civil wars; Sandinistas and Contras accept it, with free elections set for 1990.

events.title: Gorbachev fires Yeltsin
events.note: Moscow party boss Yeltsin threatens to quit over the slow pace of change and is dismissed by Gorbachev, setting up a lasting rivalry.

events.title: Washington summit and INF Treaty
events.note: On his first US visit Gorbachev signs away most intermediate-range missiles, promises an Afghan pullout and opens joint work on regional conflicts.

events.title: Nina Andreeva letter
events.note: A chemistry lecturer's letter to a newspaper defending orthodox Marxism voices widespread conservative dismay at the speed of glasnost.

events.title: Battle of Cuito Cuanavale
events.note: South Africa's 1987 push into Angola stalls as Cuban and Angolan troops hold out in Africa's biggest battle since 1945; white opinion turns against Botha's war.

events.title: Geneva Accords on Afghanistan
events.note: Pakistan and Afghanistan sign accords backed by both superpowers; Moscow pledges to leave by May 1989, yet US arms to the mujahedin keep flowing.

events.title: Reagan in Moscow
events.note: Reagan hails a new partnership on Soviet television and disowns his 'evil empire' label, but brushes off Gorbachev's pleas for cooperation on regional conflicts.

events.title: Mandela 70th birthday concert
events.note: A Wembley concert for the jailed ANC leader draws a global TV audience of hundreds of millions, making it harder to paint Mandela as a Communist.

events.title: Bin Laden founds al-Qaeda
events.note: As the Soviets begin leaving, bin Laden builds his own network among the internationalist Islamists gathered in Afghanistan and Pakistan.

events.title: Pinochet loses plebiscite
events.note: Pinochet unexpectedly loses a vote meant to rubber-stamp his rule; debt-battered middle classes now value legality over anti-Left rhetoric.

events.title: First Kohl-Gorbachev meeting
events.note: East German objections and Kohl's suspicion, including a jibe likening Gorbachev to Goebbels, delay a proper meeting until late 1988.

events.title: Bush elected president
events.note: Reagan's vice president wins, a sign voters have forgiven Iran-Contra; a more traditional Cold Warrior, Bush opens with a cautious pause in Soviet policy that disappoints Gorbachev.

events.title: Angola-Namibia accords
events.note: Superpower cooperation yields a linked deal: Cuban troops leave Angola and Namibia becomes independent; Westad sees a peak of Third World conflict resolution.

events.title: Polish Round Table talks
events.note: After strikes and Wałęsa's televised rout of an official, the regime bargains with Solidarity, agreeing to legalize it and hold partly free elections.

events.title: Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan
events.note: The last Soviet soldiers leave ahead of schedule; the civil war continues, but Gorbachev draws a line under a costly fiasco.

events.title: First contested Soviet elections
events.note: Polls for the Congress of People's Deputies break the party's monopoly: about a fifth of seats go to independents such as Sakharov and the ousted Yeltsin.

events.title: Gorbachev visits Castro in Havana
events.note: Leaving their Angola quarrel aside, the two back a Central American settlement; Castro wants Cuba out before Soviet support fades.

events.title: Thatcher hosts Gorbachev in London
events.note: While Bush pauses to rethink Soviet policy, Thatcher heaps praise on Gorbachev and urges him to keep going with reform.

events.title: Gorbachev in Beijing
events.note: The first Soviet leader's visit in three decades normalizes relations, but student protests on Tiananmen overshadow it; Deng concedes errors on both sides.

events.title: Hungary opens its border with Austria
events.note: Having legalized some opposition groups, Budapest lifts travel curbs toward Austria, making Hungarians the first Warsaw Pact citizens able to cross freely into the West.

events.title: Gorbachev talks with Willy Brandt
events.note: In talks with Brandt, by then leading the Socialist International, Gorbachev muses about healing the socialist rift of 1914 and anchoring the USSR in Europe.

events.title: Imre Nagy reburied
events.note: Budapest gives the executed 1956 leader a state reburial; Moscow raises no objection while young speakers such as Orbán denounce submission to Russia.

events.title: Solidarity sweeps Polish elections
events.note: Solidarity takes all but one contested Sejm seat and 99 of 100 in the Senate, humiliating the Communists on the day of the Beijing massacre.

events.title: Tiananmen Square crackdown
events.note: Deng sends tanks against weeks of pro-democracy protest; hundreds die and Zhao is purged, yet Washington avoids isolating a China it still needs against Moscow.

events.title: Gorbachev renounces interference in allies
events.note: At the Council of Europe Gorbachev says each people picks its own system, signalling that Moscow will live with a non-Communist Poland.

events.title: Baltic Way human chain
events.note: Estonians, Latvians and Lithuanians join hands across their republics demanding freedom; by December Lithuania's Communists have broken with the CPSU.

events.title: Poland's first non-Communist government
events.note: The Communists give up and the Sejm elects Solidarity's Mazowiecki premier; Moscow declares it a purely Polish affair.

events.title: Hungary lets East Germans go west
events.note: Partly for humanitarian reasons and partly for West German credit, Budapest lets hundreds of East German refugees into Austria, infuriating Honecker.

events.title: Vietnam leaves Cambodia
events.note: Squeezed by China and ASEAN, Hanoi pulls out all its troops, then mends relations with Beijing and signs ASEAN's amity treaty by 1992.

events.title: Thatcher and Mitterrand caution Gorbachev on Germany
events.note: As East Germany stirs, both Western leaders assure Gorbachev that unification is not on the agenda; he agrees but frets over Honecker's rigidity.

events.title: Gorbachev at GDR's 40th anniversary
events.note: Gorbachev avoids open criticism in East Berlin but makes his distrust of Honecker plain; the Central Committee removes Honecker shortly afterwards.

events.title: Honecker ousted
events.note: As the Leipzig marches swell after Gorbachev's cool anniversary visit, the SED Central Committee drops its leader; successor Krenz offers talks with the opposition and easier travel west.

events.title: Hungary ends Communist rule
events.note: The ruling party dissolves itself and the people's republic, relaunching as Socialists ahead of free elections; the Kremlin, unlike in 1956, sends congratulations.

events.title: Leipzig Monday demonstrations
events.note: Church-rooted protests swell from 70,000 to over 300,000 marchers within weeks as the security forces give up trying to stop them.

events.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
events.note: After Schabowski's garbled 9 November press conference, crowds surge to the crossings and overwhelmed guards open them; Westad sees this unplanned opening as 1989's decisive breakthrough.

events.title: Kohl's ten-point plan for unity
events.note: Kohl sets out a route to German unity embedded in European integration; Bush promptly endorses it, leaving Thatcher isolated.

events.title: Velvet Revolution
events.note: Mass protests and Havel's Civic Forum topple Czechoslovakia's leadership; Dubček rejoins the crowds, and by year's end Havel is president.

events.title: Lithuanian Communists break with Moscow
events.note: Just after the Malta summit, Lithuania's party declares itself independent of the CPSU, wagering that siding with the national movement is its only way to stay relevant.

events.title: Malta summit
events.note: Bush and Gorbachev agree the Cold War is over but read it differently: Bush presses on Nicaragua and Cuba, Gorbachev speaks of moving beyond force.

events.title: Romanian revolution
events.note: Unrest spreads from Timişoara to Bucharest, where crowds heckle Ceauşescu on live broadcast; he flees, is captured and shot with his wife on Christmas Day.

events.title: Soviet troops storm Baku
events.note: After months of Azeri-Armenian bloodshed over Nagorno-Karabakh, special forces seize Azerbaijan's capital, killing over a hundred civilians, yet the republic keeps drifting toward sovereignty.

events.title: Mitterrand and Thatcher on Germany
events.note: Mitterrand stokes Thatcher's fears of German power in private while publicly backing German self-determination and seeking monetary union in return.

events.title: Slovene and Croat Communists quit federal party
events.note: Recoiling from Milošević's Serb nationalism, the Slovenian and Croatian parties leave the Yugoslav Communist party; April elections then give both republics non-Communist majorities.

events.title: Nicaragua's free elections
events.note: Under the regional peace plan that Castro and Gorbachev endorse, the Sandinistas accept free elections in 1990 while the Contras disarm; the vote ends Sandinista rule.

events.title: East German free election
events.note: As their economy seizes up, over 40 percent of East Germans vote for Kohl's CDU to speed unity, turning it into an immediate question.

events.title: Lithuania declares independence
events.note: After non-Communists win the Baltic elections, Lithuania restores its statehood unanimously; Estonia and Latvia issue similar declarations by May.

events.title: Moscow admits Katyn massacre
events.note: After decades of denial the Soviet government accepts guilt for killing Polish officers, which Gorbachev brands a grave Stalinist crime.

events.title: Russian sovereignty declaration
events.note: Made chairman of Russia's assembly, Yeltsin has the republic put its laws above Soviet ones, then quits the Communist Party with a flourish.

events.title: Kohl and Gorbachev settle Germany
events.note: Meeting near Stavropol, the two confirm Gorbachev's surprise acceptance of a united Germany inside NATO, eased by promises of West German aid.

events.title: Iraq invades Kuwait
events.note: Saddam's grab of Kuwait sets off the first big crisis after the Cold War; Gorbachev presses his old ally to pull out, then lines up with Washington once fighting starts.

events.title: Two-Plus-Four Treaty
events.note: With British objections fudged, the two German states and the four wartime victors sign the settlement restoring full German sovereignty.

events.title: German reunification
events.note: After currency union and East Berlin's request to join the Federal Republic, Germany becomes a single democratic state again.

events.title: Shevardnadze resigns, warning of dictatorship
events.note: When Gorbachev picks the hardline Ianaev as vice president, his foreign minister quits in public protest, predicting a dictatorship; many other reformers leave in early 1991.

events.title: Soviet crackdown in the Baltics
events.note: Gorbachev's renewed use of force draws joint protest from Russia and Ukraine; Yeltsin flies to Tallinn, recognizes Baltic independence and urges soldiers to disobey.

events.title: Gulf War
events.note: After Saddam's seizure of Kuwait, Gorbachev tries to avert war but then backs the American campaign against Moscow's former ally.

events.title: Referendum on preserving the Soviet Union
events.note: Gorbachev asks voters to back a renewed federation; the Balts, Georgians and Armenians boycott, but big majorities elsewhere, even in Ukraine and Central Asia, say yes.

events.title: Japan enters slow growth
events.note: Deprived of the trade advantages the Cold War had given it, Japan stagnates, yet from a level still well above US per capita income.

events.title: Yeltsin elected Russian president
events.note: Russians give Gorbachev's chief rival a popular mandate, yet Bush keeps his distance from Yeltsin, putting Soviet stability and control of nuclear arsenals first.

events.title: Yugoslavia breaks apart
events.note: Milošević's Serb nationalism speeds the split; Slovenia and Croatia, encouraged by Germany, declare independence, opening a decade of wars killing 140,000.

events.title: Failed August coup
events.note: Hardliners hold Gorbachev in Crimea and declare an emergency; Yeltsin rallies resistance from atop a tank outside the Russian parliament, and the plot collapses in three days.

events.title: Baltic states regain independence
events.note: Amid the coup the three Baltic republics re-establish full statehood; Central Asian elites declare sovereignty over the autumn.

events.title: Bush's 'Chicken Kiev' speech
events.note: In the Ukrainian capital Bush warns against seeking independence and backs Gorbachev's union, angering nationalists; for Washington a Soviet collapse has become the bigger danger.

events.title: Yeltsin suspends the Communist Party
events.note: Yeltsin halts CPSU activity in Russia and humiliates Gorbachev in the Russian parliament, making him read proof of his colleagues' treachery.

events.title: Cambodian peace settlement
events.note: With Vietnamese troops gone and the US and China ending their support for the Khmer Rouge-led resistance, Cambodia's war is wound down in a 1991 settlement.

events.title: Vietnam normalizes relations with China
events.note: Out of Cambodia and no longer counting on Moscow, Hanoi restores ties with Beijing and soon signs ASEAN's amity treaty, recasting itself as a Southeast Asian neighbour.

events.title: Belavezha Accords
events.note: After Ukraine votes for independence, the Russian, Ukrainian and Belarusian leaders meet secretly, declare the USSR defunct and found a Commonwealth of Independent States.

events.title: Gorbachev resigns; USSR dissolves
events.note: Refusing to hold the union by force, Gorbachev phones Bush and resigns on Christmas Day; nuclear command passes to Yeltsin and the Cold War system is gone.

events.title: Ukraine votes for independence
events.note: On 1 December Ukrainians vote overwhelmingly to leave, stripping the union of its second Slavic pillar and sealing its fate a week before the Belavezha meeting.

events.title: Deng's southern tour
events.note: Aged 88, Deng tours the southern provinces to relaunch market reform, showing that repression had not halted China's economic opening.

events.title: Mujahedin take Kabul
events.note: Najibullah outlasts the Soviet exit until supplies dry up; the victorious mujahedin then fight each other, and Hekmatyar shells the capital.

events.title: Russia's shock privatization
events.note: Under Yeltsin, state industry and resources go to a well-connected new oligarchy—Westad calls it the raid of the century—while unemployment and mortality soar.

events.title: Putin's authoritarian Russia
events.note: Exploiting Russian feelings of exclusion, Putin blames the country's woes on American design and rules with real popular support, Westad writes.

events.title: September 11 attacks
events.note: Islamist militants from a splinter of a former US Cold War partnership strike New York and Washington, prompting a response shaped by Cold War habits.

events.title: US invades Afghanistan
events.note: Rather than targeted strikes and police cooperation, Washington occupies Afghanistan, a move Westad judges strategically pointless and likely to breed more militancy.

events.title: US invades Iraq
events.note: Advisers steeped in Cold War thinking use the unipolar moment for regime change in Iraq, which Westad counts among America's needless distant wars.

events.title: NATO and EU expand to Russia's borders
events.note: Western military and economic integration reaches Russia's frontier while Russia stays outside; Westad argues the door to Moscow should have been kept open.
